# Fixed Issues

Record of resolved kicad-happy analyzer bugs (KH-*) and test harness issues (TH-*).
Shows what changed, where, and how it was verified — useful for cross-referencing
regressions, understanding analyzer evolution, and onboarding collaborators.

> **Protocol**: When fixing issues, remove them from [ISSUES.md](ISSUES.md) and add here
> in the same session. Each entry must include: root cause, fix description, and
> verification results. See README.md "Issue tracking protocol" for full details.
> Open issues are in [ISSUES.md](ISSUES.md).

---

## 2026-11-11 — TH-063: a test spawned a mutating runner against the live tree (16,909 EMC outputs rewritten)

**Severity:** LOW
**File:** `tests/test_collection_policy.py`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-14, H0 plan 2 Task 6 (the pool-survival mechanism was TH-067, fixed)

**Fix:** the closing condition from the entry: the collection-policy audit now checks runner subprocesses. `test_runner_subprocesses_redirect_the_data_dir` walks every test file; any Python subprocess whose argv, enclosing function (with its parametrize list) or calling helper names a corpus-writing entry point (`run_{schematic,pcb,gerbers,spice,emc,thermal,datasheets}.py`, `discover.py`, `harness.py`, `checkout.py`, `retire_orphan_outputs.py`) must set `KICAD_HAPPY_TESTHARNESS_DATA_DIR`: inline in `env=`, through a local env built in the function, a module-level env dict or a module helper, or by `monkeypatch.setenv`. `git` / `ngspice` calls and other scripts are out of scope.

**Verification:** synthetic sources: a bare spawn, an env without the data dir and a parametrized script name are flagged; the five redirect styles in use are accepted. Real tree: 0 offenders; with the token stripped from every file the audit flags 19 functions in 9 files, every runner-spawning test the tree has. Tiers vs product_6138b12 3,762 / 0 / 8 / 3.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-049: an unscoped full-corpus sweep partly rewrote results/outputs between regens (writer unidentified)

**Severity:** LOW
**File:** the corpus runners' selection (`harnesslib/selection.py`)
**Discovered:** 2026-09-01, v2.2.1 regen before-baseline

**Fix:** fix direction (b) is in place: every corpus-writing entry point refuses an unscoped run without an explicit `--all` (`resolve_repos_with_source(..., require_explicit_all=True)`: `utils.run_analyzer` for schematic / pcb / gerber at `utils.py:632`, `run/_chained.py` for emc / thermal / spice, `run/run_datasheets.py`, `tools/retire_orphan_outputs.py`, `regression/run_corpus_gate.py`), and tests that spawn a runner must redirect the data dir (TH-063). The writer was never identified, and the tripwire (post-regen failures clustered on alphabetically early repos with fresh mtimes but stale run ids) did not fire at any of the eight regens and relocks since (v2.3.0 through the v3.0.1 regen at `4c2a0d6`), each with a fully attributed after-check.

**Verification:** `tests/test_harnesslib_selection.py`, `tests/test_run_chained_execution.py::test_unqualified_runs_exit_2_without_all`, `tests/test_run_spice_isolation.py::test_unqualified_run_exits_2_without_all`, `tests/test_runner_failure_exit.py` (no selector exits 2).

## 2026-11-11 — TH-109: FND locks whose check could not fail or read the wrong finding (144 live / 467 with the aspirational ones)

**Severity:** MEDIUM (each passed whatever the analyzer did; several hid defects still present)
**File:** `regression/checks.py` (`assertion_errors`, `evaluate_assertion`); data under `reference/**/assertions/` (FND locks)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-06, TH-105 triage

**Root cause:** `contains_match` / `not_contains_match` / `count_matches` read `field` + `pattern` only, so a regex left under `value` compiled `""` and matched anything; a `range` without bounds read 0..inf; `findings[<n>]` with a `detector_filter` indexed the unfiltered list.

**Fix:**
- Remapped in three passes, each checked against the lock's description: 50 mechanical R1-R4 remaps (4 found inverted and corrected), 172 triaged locks + 36 split assertions with the new `where: {field: regex}` / `field: "."` match keys, then the held set per the product's rulings (LOG `[main-repo] 2026-11-11 — TH-109 RULINGS`): 82 lock records on 61 files. 19 live locks that describe a present defect became aspirational with a real check (KH-1073..1079 filed for the classes the ruling named); 27 retired (the 23 ruled, FND-00001445-AST-11, FND-00001389-AST-04 once G1/G2/G4 were found `in_bom=yes`, and the KH-1070 pair FND-00001904-AST-05 / FND-00002289-AST-03 by analogy with FND-00002228-AST-02); 16 graduated (5 FND, FND-00001461-AST-04 on `^3\.3V$`, 8 TH-107 re-pointed siderakb / keebio sets, FND-00002192-AST-02 with a real courtyard check plus its split FND-00002192-AST-03, and FND-00001457-AST-09 overruled to live); FND-00000395-AST-01 and FND-00000442-AST-06 re-anchored live by ref. Four locks the ruling made aspirational did not describe a present defect when the analyzer was re-run at `6138b126` (kicad-cli 10.0.8 for the netlist one) and were re-anchored live instead: FND-00000417-AST-06 (LED audit D2 → R8), FND-00001642-AST-07 (J1 CC role sink), FND-00000386-AST-03 (R2 pin 1 is on the Q1 collector net; the description had the 180° pins backwards), FND-00001498-AST-05 (AP3012 is this project's U5, output 5V). Not graduated although they pass: FND-00002186-AST-02 (min_count over all findings, vacuous), FND-00002188-AST-02 and FND-00002191-AST-01 (unclear intent); FND-00000425-AST-04 stays aspirational (withdrawn).
- Guard (`assertion_errors`): a regex op with neither `pattern` nor a non-empty `where`, and a `range` with neither `min` nor `max`, are load errors; `findings[<n>]` with a `detector_filter` filters, then indexes. Tests `tests/test_th109_check_shapes.py` (20).

**Verification:** on the 56 touched repos hard 13,795 → 13,791 / 0 failed / 0 load errors, every transition reconciled per lock (records `results/th109/rulings/`: `apply_rulings.py`, `applied.json`, `before.json` / `after.json`); mutation check 32 / 32 live checks fail on a mutated output. Full corpus with the guard `--era all`: 2,717,768 / 2,717,768, 0 errors, 0 load errors, aspirational 525 passing of 1,883 (`full_guard.json`). Tiers vs product_6138b12 3,759 / 0 / 8 / 3.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-064: emc / thermal / spice runners had no identity-based `--resume`

**Severity:** LOW (the flag was refused, so nothing ran on stale identity)
**File:** `run/run_emc.py`, `run/run_thermal.py`, `run/run_spice.py`, `run/_chained.py`, `harnesslib/batch.py`, `harness.py`, `regression/compare_spice_offline.py`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-15, H0 plan 2 final review

**Fix:** `harnesslib.batch.start_run` is `run_batch`'s manifest lifecycle moved out unchanged (write the manifest, keep the prior run_id on a matched resume, otherwise archive `units.jsonl`); `run/_chained.ChainedRun` gives the three chained runners a manifest + per-unit records keyed by output path (`owner/repo/<output>`). A unit's input sha covers the upstream outputs it reads (schematic; + pcb for emc / thermal and for spice `--with-parasitics`). A unit is reused only under the matched run, with an `ok` record and its output unchanged. `map_units` records each result as it finishes (`on_result`). `harness.py run` passes `--resume` to spice / emc again; `compare_spice_offline` ignores the root `manifest.json`. The chained runners now need the product to be a git worktree, as `run_batch` already did (gate clones and the spice-offline lane use clones). Argv is part of the identity, so `--jobs` / `--timeout` changes disable resume.

**Verification:** `tests/test_chained_resume.py` (reuse; rerun on upstream / product / argv / output / failed-record / run_id change; log archive; no prior manifest; `--jobs 2` logs every unit), refusal test replaced; an A/B of old vs new runners on fake data gave byte-identical analyzer outputs, `.parasitics.json` and `_aggregate.json` on the non-resume path. Tiers vs product_6138b12 3,759 / 0 / 8 / 3.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-111: a check path cannot reach a net whose name contains a dot (`nets.+3.3V.pins`)

**Severity:** LOW (FND locks on dotted net names can never resolve; met in the TH-109 triage, worked around where the net was renamed, e.g. hawk `+3V3`)
**File:** `utils.resolve_path` (splits the path on `.`), used by `regression/checks.py` `evaluate_assertion`; also `where` field names
**Discovered:** 2026-11-11, TH-109 triage (batches 3 and 4: FND-00001479-AST-04 on `3.3V`)

**Symptom:** `nets.+3.3V.pins` splits into `nets`, `+3`, `3V`, `pins`; the lock resolves to nothing and fails (or passes, under a `not_*` op) whatever the analyzer does.

**Fix direction:** a quoted or bracketed segment (`nets["+3.3V"].pins`) in `resolve_path`, with a load error for a path whose first segment names a dict whose keys contain dots; or a `match` on `nets` items by name.

- **Fix:** a quoted key segment: `nets["+3.3V"].pins`. `utils.split_quoted_path` tokenizes paths that contain `["` (quoted keys may hold dots, `\"` escapes a quote, `[n]` indexes lists); `resolve_path` uses it only for such paths, so every existing path resolves as before. `regression/checks.py` `_item_field` / `_item_path` accept the same syntax for `field`, `where` keys and `field_equals` match / assert fields. No load-time guard for unquoted dotted names (not needed: no corpus lock path or field uses `["` today, and the TH-109 locks that met this were written against renamed nets or `where`).
- **Verification:** `tests/test_utils.py` (5 new: dotted key, quoted key then index, quoted first segment / missing, escaped quote, unquoted path unchanged) and `tests/test_checks_where.py::test_quoted_field_names_reach_dotted_keys` red before, green after; checks / run_checks / required-field tests 119 passed; corpus scan: 0 assertion paths or fields contain `["`.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-110: `audit_constants.py` gives a new constant the lowest free `CONST-NNN`, so a retired id is reused for an unrelated constant

**Severity:** LOW (no tracked doc cites the reused ids today; registry history and any old `CONST-NNN` reference then point at two different constants)
**File:** `validate/audit_constants.py:338-349` `_next_id` (gap-filling `while n in existing`), called from `update_registry` `:555`
**Discovered:** 2026-11-07, registry rescan at product `f53d107e` (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate)

**Symptom:** the rescan retired 8 constants and added 19; six of the new ones took old ids: `CONST-301` `_ISOLATION_RAIL_EVIDENCE`, `CONST-388` `_LTC23_RESOLUTION_SUFFIX`, `CONST-560` `radio_words`, `CONST-690` `_CONNECTOR_WORDS`, `CONST-691` `_DEVICE_PASSIVE_SYMBOL`, `CONST-969` `_USB_SIGNAL_NAME`. `CONST-560` belonged to a different constant in earlier registries (`git log -S'"CONST-560"' -- reference/constants_registry.json`).

**Fix direction:** keep a high-water mark (`next_id` in the registry header, or max id + 1) and never reuse a number, as KH/TH ids are never reused.

- **Root cause:** `_next_id` took the lowest free `CONST-NNN`, and retired constants are deleted from the registry, so a retired id went to an unrelated new constant (CONST-301/388/560/690/691/969 at the f53d107 rescan).
- **Fix:** the registry stores a `next_id` high-water mark, which `update_registry` records before retiring entries; ids come from the larger of the mark and the highest current id + 1. A registry without the field starts at its highest id + 1 = CONST-1018, which is also the highest id in the registry's git history (45 versions). The next rescan adds the field.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_audit_constants_ids.py` (gap not refilled, retired highest id not reissued, stored mark honoured, ids distinct within one scan) failed 4 of 5 before the fix and passes after; the existing audit_constants tests pass.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-061: `tests/test_datasheet_db_cli.py` plants and deletes a file under `HARNESS_DIR/repos/.test_fallback/` — a write into the corpus checkout tree

**Severity:** LOW (corpus inputs must be immutable; the fixture cleans up after
itself, but a crash between plant and delete leaves a stray dir in `repos/`)
**File:** `tests/test_datasheet_db_cli.py` (~lines 481-527, the `.test_fallback`
fixture)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-14, H0 plan 1 Task 4 corpus-marker audit.

**Fix direction:** point the fallback fixture at `tmp_path` and monkeypatch the
CLI's repos root, so no test writes into `repos/`.

- **Root cause:** `validate/datasheet_db/cli.py` `_try_found_in_fallback` resolved `repo` found_in refs against a hard-coded `HARNESS_DIR / "repos"` instead of `storage.REPOS_DIR` (the root `insert --scan-repos` records refs against, which follows `KICAD_HAPPY_TESTHARNESS_DATA_DIR` / `DATASHEET_DB_REPOS_DIR`), so the test had to plant a file in the live corpus tree.
- **Fix:** the fallback uses `REPOS_DIR`; the test plants under a tmp tree, redirects `storage.REPOS_DIR`, and asserts `HARNESS_DIR/repos/.test_fallback` never appears. The `preserved` branch still reads `HARNESS_DIR / "datasheets_from_repos"` (out of scope).
- **Verification:** the rewritten test failed against the old CLI and passes after; 115 datasheet_db tests and `test_collection_policy` pass.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-068: fixture-lane A/A cannot strict-verify chained envelopes after the basetemp tree is moved

**Severity:** LOW (the corpus lanes prove the chained analyzers strict-clean at scale; only the offline fixture lane is affected)
**File:** `tools/aa_run.py` (`snapify`, `--fixture-trees`), RUNBOOK/plan-6 Task 7 Step 4 recipe
**Discovered:** 2026-10-15, H0 plan 6 Task 7 Step 4

**Symptom:** emc / thermal / cross_analysis envelopes embed ABSOLUTE upstream paths
(`inputs.source_hashes` keys, `upstream_artifacts[].path`) under the pytest basetemp.
The recipe runs the contract suite twice at the same basetemp and moves the tree aside
between runs, so verify-then-mask (`sha256_of` / `strip_root_prefix_keys`) cannot read
the upstream file → "linked file missing", 36 violations / 18 source_hashes deltas on the
9 chained units; the 12 non-chained units are identical.

**Fix direction:** `snapify` re-roots chained upstream references into the snapified
tree (or the recipe keeps both basetemps in place and passes them as root prefixes), so
the fixture lane covers all six analyzers in strict mode.

- **Root cause:** emc / thermal / cross_analysis envelopes name their upstream schematic / pcb envelopes by absolute basetemp path; after the recipe moved the tree aside the comparator could not open them ("linked file missing"), and run-dir names inside the paths differed between sessions.
- **Fix:** `tools/aa_run.py` `snapify` rewrites absolute paths in `inputs` that end in an envelope of the tree to that upstream's byte-exact `snap.json` (longest suffix match); envelopes that need no rewrite are copied byte for byte, so the recorded sha256 still verifies. A chained envelope used as another chained analyzer's upstream would be re-serialized and fail loudly as a policy violation. `summarize_strict_report` also reads a report whose deltas sit in a `deltas_file` sidecar (TH-096).
- **Verification:** the real contract-suite fixture lane went from 36 violations / 54 deltas on 9 chained units to 21 / 21 identical with 0 violations; a tampered hash still errors (exit 2). `tests/test_aa_run.py` 30 / 30 (4 new).

## 2026-11-11 — TH-096: the gate's field comparator keeps every delta in memory and writes them all — an output-changing round of ~55 M deltas exhausts a 62 GB box

**Severity:** MEDIUM (blocks the mechanical verdict on large output-changing rounds; the box is shared)
**File:** `regression/field_compare.py` (`compare_trees` accumulates `deltas` and serialises `[d.to_json() for d in deltas]`; `budgeted_report` rebuilds every `Delta`); `regression/run_corpus_gate.py` (`run_modes` runs the comparator with the gate's `--jobs`); `regression/compare_snap_trees.py`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-26, product 3.0.x Wave 3 gate (`results/v30x_w3_gate/`)

**Symptom:** after phases A/B finished, the in-process comparator's 32 workers reached ~67 GB summed RSS, swap climbed 17 → 20.6 GB in 30 s with ~10 GB available; the run was stopped by hand (SIGTERM to its process group, `results/v30x_w3_gate_aux/operations.log`). Sampled estimate: ~55 M strict deltas on schematic units (3,445 per moved unit × 15,884) and ~1.8 M on pcb, before the chained analyzers. No `field_report_*.json` was written. The verdict was produced instead by `results/v30x_w3_gate_aux/stream_budgeted.py` (same `compare_strict` / `evaluate_budget` per unit, counts only), valid because the Wave 3 budget has no `unit_bound` / `expected_magnitude`.

**Fix direction:** stream deltas to a JSONL file and keep counts in memory; evaluate the budget per unit when no class carries a cross-unit bound (bounds can aggregate claimed counts per class); give the comparator its own worker cap.

- **Fix:** comparator workers spool each unit's deltas to a scratch file and return only counts, at most 4 units per worker in flight, taken in completion order; the report is rebuilt in sorted unit order (byte-identical for any `--jobs`). The budget is evaluated per unit inside the workers (`field_compare.compare_budgeted`), with unit bounds and magnitudes summed over units. Up to `INLINE_DELTAS_MAX` (200,000) deltas the report keeps its inline lists (`deltas_file: null`); above it `deltas`, `budget.claimed` and `budget.residuals` are null and the lists sit in `<stem>.deltas.jsonl`, `.residuals.jsonl` and per-unit `.claims.jsonl` sidecars named in the report; `budget.residual_count` is always present; read with `field_compare.iter_report_deltas`. The gate has `--compare-jobs` (default `min(--jobs, 8)`); `compare_snap_trees.py --jobs` defaults to `min(cpu, 8)`. Budget predicates v30x_wave2/3/4a read `units[].delta_count` instead of `len(report["deltas"])`; `run_modes` deletes stale `field_report_*.json` first; `generate_validation_md` follows `claims_file`; `aa_run` follows `deltas_file`. The `stream_budgeted.py` copies under `results/*_aux/` are superseded.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_field_compare_streaming.py` (11) plus the comparator, budget, gate and validation tests, 568 passed. The w11b2 std gate re-compared ALL MATCH against the recorded report (149,633 units, 196,210 deltas, all residual under the draft budget, complete delta and residual lists) both inline and with sidecars forced, 10:56 vs 14:05 before; fc ALL MATCH (21,411 units, 37,839 deltas). Synthetic 3 M-delta tree: parent 39 MB (old code 9.3 GB). Whole-tree peak on std inline 15.0 GB vs 13.9 GB is the per-worker high-water of the largest units (about 6 GB each, the same as before), not deltas; lower `--compare-jobs` to cut it. `generate_validation_md` output is byte-identical before and after on the v3.0.2 draft's recorded arguments.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-099: emc / thermal can pair a schematic with an orphan pcb output left over from the pre-hash output naming

**Severity:** LOW (one corpus unit at the 40b8ff3 relock)
**File:** `results/outputs/pcb/` hygiene; the chained runners' sch↔pcb pairing (`run/run_emc.py`, `run/run_thermal.py`) reads any pcb output whose name matches, fresh or not
**Discovered:** 2026-10-29, 3.0.x relock at 40b8ff3 (`results/v30x_w4b_relock/`)

**Symptom:** 93 pcb outputs (81 repos) were not rewritten by the relock because no manifest unit maps to their names any more (outputs named before long output names were hashed). The emc and thermal runners still pair one schematic with one of them: hmaerki/experiment_microoctopus `…Raspberry Pi Zero W.sch` reads `…Raspberry Pi Zero W.kicad_pcb.json` (2026-04-09) while the fresh `…Raspberry Pi Z_b81a647b03.json` exists. The same unit in the gate tree pairs with nothing. The emc runner already retires orphan emc / spice outputs whose schematic output is gone (`RETIRED … schematic output missing/stale`); pcb and gerber orphans (93 / 10) are not retired.

**Fix direction:** retire pcb and gerber outputs that map to no manifest unit (same `.stale` rename as the emc runner), and have the chained runners pair only with outputs whose source is in the current manifest.

- **Fix:** `utils.find_pcb_output` returns a pcb output only if a unit in the repo's `pcbs.txt` manifest writes that file name (plain name swap and the hash-truncated lookup alike; no manifest, no pairing), so emc, thermal and `run_spice --with-parasitics` match the gate's `_pcb_key_for` pairing. New `tools/retire_orphan_outputs.py` lists outputs no manifest unit writes and renames them `.stale` (reuses `utils.retire_orphaned_outputs`, which gained `apply=`); dry-run unless `--apply`, needs a selector or `--all`, exit 2 on a missing manifest.
- **Census (2026-11-11, live tree, not applied):** orphans schematic 0 / pcb 29 (17 repos) / gerber 7 (5 repos), down from 93 / 10 at 40b8ff3; 2 of the pcb orphans sit in pre-owner pseudo-repo dirs (`Arduino_OpenTherm_shield`, `Mechanical-Keyboard`). Mis-paired today: 1 emc + 1 thermal unit (the hmaerki Raspberry Pi Zero W unit), now unpaired. Run `tools/retire_orphan_outputs.py --all --apply` at the next corpus regen.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_th099_orphan_outputs.py` (9, every subprocess under a tmp data dir) plus the chained / spice runner tests, 101 passed; 0 `.stale` files in the live tree before and after.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-101: no gate profile exercises gerber `--full` output (`connectivity`), so the product's Wave 5 Task 52 class is gate-blind harness-side

**Severity:** LOW (not blocking; coverage gap, no wrong verdict)
**File:** `harnesslib/profiles.py` (`standard` runs gerbers without `--full`; `full-chain` declares no gerber analyzer), `regression/run_corpus_gate.py` (gerber invocation)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-31, product 3.0.x Wave 5 gate (`results/v30x_w5_gate{,_fc}`)

**Symptom:** `analyze_gerbers.py --full` adds the pin→net `connectivity` list. The Wave 5 handoff budgets a Task 52 class on it (decoded `\uXXXX` names, comment-form `TO.P`/`TO.N`, empty-ref pins dropped; 23-24 of 150 modern units in the product's A/B), but neither harness profile produces that block, so the corpus gate never compared it; the product's own A/B is the only evidence.

**Fix direction:** give a profile a gerber `--full` lane: either add gerber with `--full` to `full-chain` (cheap: ~5.5 k gerber dirs corpus-wide, a few hundred in the 260-repo sample), or a separate `gerber-full` profile over all gerber dirs. Declare it in `harnesslib.profiles`, pass `--full` in the gate's gerber invocation when the profile asks for it, and add the profile to the round-record profile list. Re-measure the Task 52 class once it exists (expect connectivity deltas only on X2-tagged dirs).

- **Fix:** `Profile.gerber_full`; `full-chain` now declares gerber with `gerber_full=True`, and `run_corpus_gate.file_cmd` passes `--full` for it. Full-chain budgets must claim gerber deltas from now on; re-measure the Wave 5 Task 52 connectivity class at the next full-chain gate.
- **Verification:** `tests/test_harnesslib_profiles.py` and `tests/test_run_corpus_gate_phase_a.py` failed before and pass after; gate tests 195 passed. No gate run yet.

## 2026-11-11 — TH-107: 34 aspirational assertions (27 sets) never run because their output file is not found

**Severity:** LOW (aspirational only; they fail as "output file not found" forever, so they can never graduate)
**File:** data under `reference/**/assertions/` (list below); `regression/reference_io.py` `find_output_file`
**Discovered:** 2026-11-06, v3.0.2 kickoff. The two counted errors (doubled `file_pattern` prefix) are fixed (FIXED.md, same date), and `run_checks` now reports `output_not_found` (JSON) / an "Output not found" line, so the class is visible.

**Remaining sets, by disposition:**
- **Re-point (11 sets, output exists under another project):** the assertion file sits under the wrong project dir with an old `schematic_<repo>_` / `pcb_<repo>_` pattern. siderakb/ergo-snm-keyboard: 9 sets filed under `EC56_rotary_encoder_pcb` (FND-00002185..2193; outputs `ErgoSNM_Keyboard_rev*_*.json`); keebio/fourier: 1 under `fourier_fourier-left_fourier-left-bottom` (FND-00002181, output `fourier_fourier-right_fourier-right.sch.json`); rjwalters/kicad-tools: 1 under `boards_01-voltage-divider_output_voltage_divider` (output `examples_08-label-based-schematic_label_based_mcu.kicad_sch.json`). Their `findings.json` items carry the same wrong file names, so a fix moves item + assertions together (or `findings.py promote` recreates the bad files).
- **Retire (3 sets):** 0Prashant/Kicad FND-00002472/2473/2475/2476: the findings name files under `schematic/MyKiCad/`, another repo; the files do not exist in 0Prashant/Kicad.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-436: `test_coverage` counts `Connector:TestPoint`-based touch pads as test points


**Severity:** LOW (coverage metric inflated on capacitive-touch boards; same footprint family KH-373/413 already classify as touch pads)

**Gate budget (when fixed):** `test_coverage` counts shrink on touch-pad boards (CP-003 population).

**Rider (2026-11-03, soak run 10):** the PCB TE-001 census has the same blind spot (`pcb/assembly.py` `_is_test_point`, reference prefix) — filed separately as KH-895.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** test_coverage, TE-001 and FD-001 counted capacitive touch pads as test points or SMD parts. The test-point half was fixed in Waves 9b+9c; FD-001 now skips footprints the touch classifier names by footprint alone, so a connector valued `Touch` is still counted.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-441: via-analysis `via_in_pad` attributes a via to the FIRST pad whose outline contains it — ambiguous on footprints where a pin pad's rotated extent and the exposed pad both contain the via (attribution + `same_net` flip with pad order)


**Severity:** LOW (fact-field attribution; surfaced by the KH-419 outline test
at the soak-fix gate: 879 entries re-attributed and 678 `same_net` flips on
the 2,057 moved units, e.g. Thinkpad U2 via (35.4, 31.7) is inside both the
unnumbered exposed pad and pad 57 at 45° and now reports pad `""` /
`same_net: false` instead of `57` / `true`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analyze_pcb.py` (`analyze_vias` via-in-pad
loop, `break` on first containing pad)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-06, harness soak-fix gate 9fbbb26 → ef6d55c
(`results/v23x_soak_gate/adjudication_soak.md`)

**Fix direction:** when several pads contain the via, prefer the pad on the
via's net, then the smallest pad (the exposed pad's bounding rect swallows
pin pads on rotated QFN/DFN footprints); report `pad: ""` only when no
numbered pad contains the via. Fixture: a QFN at 45° with a via on a pin pad
that also falls inside the exposed-pad rectangle.

**Gate budget (when fixed):** `via_in_pad[].pad` / `same_net` on rotated
QFN/DFN boards (subset of the KH-419 class); VP-001 unaffected.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** via_in_pad attributed a via to the first pad whose outline held it, so on a rotated QFN the exposed-pad rectangle or a pin pad won by pad order. The holder is now chosen by net, then numbered pad, then size.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev c0af4ac4 (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `pcb/copper.py:461-477`: every pad holding the via is collected, then the pad on the via's net, then a numbered pad, then the smallest is taken; one entry per via.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2 whole-range gate `0f2deade..6138b126` vs `product_f53d107` (ledger `f53d107.json`), 2026-11-08: standard 149,633 units + full-chain 21,411, every moved unit claimed by the per-unit judge `regression/budgets/v302_wave11b2_judge.py` (0 residual); spice-offline, text oracle, `--schema`, distributor-offline and a gerber `--full` A/B as declared (records `results/v302_w11b2_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}/`).

## 2026-11-08 — KH-457: silkscreen revision check misses `rev2` / `v1.1`-style marks with no separator — `\b(?:REV|VER|VERSION)\b|(?<!\w)[RV]\d` needs a word boundary after REV or a lone R/V


**Severity:** LOW (false `missing_revision` documentation warning → `fab_release_gate` `[WARN] No revision marking found on silkscreen` on a board whose silk reads `sacmap-rev2 (2026)`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analyze_pcb.py:3531-3541` (`rev_pattern`; consumed by `fab_release_gate.py:144-152` `revision_marking`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-22, SacMap rev2 soak run 9 (`~/Projects/sandbox/Old-Reviews/sacmap-rev2/9/`, product `main` @ `4701c26` = v2.3.2 pre-tag; report `REVIEW-2026-10-22.md`, meta `REVIEW-2026-10-22-meta.md`), report §18.6 / meta §2 #3

**Repro:** silk text `sacmap-rev2 (2026)`, empty title-block `rev`: `REV\b` fails (V is followed by `2`), `(?<!\w)[RV]\d` fails (`V` is preceded by `E`) → `has_revision False`.

**Fix direction:** `(?<![A-Z])(?:REV|VER|VERSION|R|V)\s*[-_.]?\s*\d` (case-insensitive) plus the existing word forms; keep the title-block `rev` precedence. Gate budget: `documentation_warnings` `missing_revision` disappearances corpus-wide (count at the filing round).

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The silkscreen revision regex needed a word boundary after REV or a lone R/V, so `rev2` and `v1.1` marks were missed. A digit-guarded form now reads them, and rail text stays unmatched.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 675c492f (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `pcb/reader.py:1836-1839`: the revision regex adds `(?<![A-Z0-9])(?:REV|VER|VERSION)\s*[-_.]?\s*\d` and `(?<![A-Z0-9])V\d+\.\d`. Probe: `sacmap-rev2 (2026)`, `Rev1.0`, `Ver1.0`, `board_v1.1` match; `3V3`, `5V0`, `VCC_3V3`, `SERVER2`, `LEVEL2`, `DRIVER1` do not.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2 whole-range gate `0f2deade..6138b126` vs `product_f53d107` (ledger `f53d107.json`), 2026-11-08: standard 149,633 units + full-chain 21,411, every moved unit claimed by the per-unit judge `regression/budgets/v302_wave11b2_judge.py` (0 residual); spice-offline, text oracle, `--schema`, distributor-offline and a gerber `--full` A/B as declared (records `results/v302_w11b2_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}/`).

## 2026-11-08 — KH-573: thermal-pad via adequacy (TV-001) counts vias of any net and layer, and its exemption hides an untented via in a signal pad (VP-001)


**Severity:** HIGH (TV-001 default path; feeds thermal's via correction factor)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/pcb/copper.py:648-668` (Tier-1 loop over `all_vias` with no net or layer test; only Tier 2 at `:697` checks net); `:1219-1220` (VP-001 exemption by component ref, called at `pipeline.py:484-486`); consumer `analyze_thermal.py:349-354`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R9-F2, kc/R9-F6)

**Symptom:** a 2×2 mm GND exposed pad with 5 net-99 vias at x = 1.3 (outside the pad, inside the 1.5× box) gives `via_count 5`, `adequacy adequate`, `severity info`. Thermal then applies the via correction from those foreign vias. The VP-001 exemption set holds component refs from TV-001 entries, so every SMD pad of that footprint is skipped. A QFN with an untented via in signal pad 1 gives `[]` with the exemption and `Via in pad: U1:1 (untented)` without it (`--full`).

**Fix direction / budget:** in Tier 1, count only vias on the pad's net that span the pad's layer. Exempt by `(ref, pad)` for the exposed pad only. Budget: corpus output, TV-001 `via_count` / `adequacy`, thermal via correction (Tj values), and VP-001 appearances (`--full`). Size first. This is distinct from KH-441 (via_in_pad first-pad attribution).

**Addendum 2026-11-06 (v3.0.2 survey correction):** only partly stale: TV-001's first pass still ignores the via layer span (`pcb/copper.py:678-693`); a stacked microvia chain reaching the pad is the ruled case. Lands in Wave 11b.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** TV-001 counted vias of any net and layer under a thermal pad, and VP-001 exempted every pad of a TV-001 footprint. The net test and the per-pad exemption landed earlier; the residue, the via layer span, is now checked: a via counts when its own span or a same-point stacked chain reaches the pad copper.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev ab5a08c8 (earlier halves landed before this wave) (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `pcb/copper.py:48-77` `_vias_reaching`; Tier 1 skips a via whose copper does not reach the pad layer (`:733-742`). Already present: the same-net test (`:737-739`) and the VP-001 exemption by (ref, pad) (`:1311-1331`).
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2 whole-range gate `0f2deade..6138b126` vs `product_f53d107` (ledger `f53d107.json`), 2026-11-08: standard 149,633 units + full-chain 21,411, every moved unit claimed by the per-unit judge `regression/budgets/v302_wave11b2_judge.py` (0 residual); spice-offline, text oracle, `--schema`, distributor-offline and a gerber `--full` A/B as declared (records `results/v302_w11b2_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}/`).

## 2026-11-08 — KH-658: CC-001 compares the net-wide narrowest trace, not the connector's; TW-001 applies a regulator's output current to its input rail


**Severity:** LOW
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/cross_analysis.py` (CC-001 / TW-001 after KH-566)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, product 3.0.x Wave 2 review (handoff §Asks 4g)

**Symptom:** CC-001 takes the narrowest trace anywhere on the net, so one unit got 6 findings from a single thin `+24V` segment far from the connector; TW-001 checks the input rail against the regulator's output current. Minor: CC-001 summaries state the estimated current as a fact (`~X A`; proxy capped at 1 A LDO / 2 A switcher).

**Fix direction / budget:** measure the trace attached to the connector pad, use the input current (`Iout * Vout / (Vin * eff)`) for the input rail, mark the current "(est.)". Budget: CC-001 / TW-001 on full-chain cross units (Wave 2 product estimate CC-001 6 / 1 unit, TW-001 6 / 3 units).

---

- **Root cause / fix:** CC-001 compared the narrowest trace anywhere on the net, and TW-001 loaded a regulator's input rail with its output current. CC-001 now measures the connector's own path, input rails carry Iout*Vout/(Vin*eff), and the estimated current is marked (est.).
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 11272ef9 (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `cross_analysis.py:132-142` `_reg_iin`; CC-001 takes the routed connector-to-regulator path (`_path_min_width` `:145`), else the track leaving the connector courtyard (`_attached_min_width` `:160`), else no finding; `:311` sums input current; TW-001 loads input rails with `_reg_iin` (`:1000`); both summaries end `(est.)` (`:329`, `:1023`). The net-wide minimum loop is gone.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2 whole-range gate `0f2deade..6138b126` vs `product_f53d107` (ledger `f53d107.json`), 2026-11-08: standard 149,633 units + full-chain 21,411, every moved unit claimed by the per-unit judge `regression/budgets/v302_wave11b2_judge.py` (0 residual); spice-offline, text oracle, `--schema`, distributor-offline and a gerber `--full` A/B as declared (records `results/v302_w11b2_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}/`).

**File:** `skills/spice/scripts/spice_templates.py` (transistor bench, P-channel)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-28, product 3.0.x Wave 4 Part A handoff; filed by the harness

**Symptom:** P-channel MOSFET benches report `vth_V` 0.0 because of the sweep direction, left after Task 24's `i_on` fix.

**Fix direction / budget:** sweep in the P-channel direction; budget P-ch `transistor_circuit` values under spice-offline.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The P-channel bench swept the gate from ground and measured on an `abs()` expression ngspice's `meas` does not take, so `vth_V` read 0.0; VGS is now swept from the source supply toward -VDD and the magnitude is a separate vector.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 47249a44 (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `spice_templates.py:1107-1118` P-channel bench: `VGS {gate} vdd DC 0` swept 0 to -VDD, `id = abs(i(VDD))` as its own vector, `vth` when `id` crosses 1 mA; `spice_results.py:561-562` drops `vth` with no current vector. A/B sp-pmos-vth 56 results / 38 units; product test PMOS vth about -1.56 V.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2 whole-range gate `0f2deade..6138b126` vs `product_f53d107` (ledger `f53d107.json`), 2026-11-08: standard 149,633 units + full-chain 21,411, every moved unit claimed by the per-unit judge `regression/budgets/v302_wave11b2_judge.py` (0 residual); spice-offline, text oracle, `--schema`, distributor-offline and a gerber `--full` A/B as declared (records `results/v302_w11b2_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}/`).

## 2026-11-08 — KH-722: a label-like regulator Value that parses as a part-number core makes the SPICE regulator bench `info` "the value names another part"


**Severity:** LOW (R42 e)

---

Probe: LDO1, BUCK5V, U3V3, 'DCDC24V/5V NUM' -> True; TPS61023DRLR, LM338_TO220, REG1117, SPX1117-ADJ -> False.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-928: the Gerber `*.g*` glob still reads non-Gerber files as error records


**Severity:** LOW (gerber `error` records, `layer_count` / completeness)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analyze_gerbers.py:1652` (`glob("*.gbr") + glob("*.g*")`), `:1636-1640` (`_is_repo_or_fs_artifact`: `startswith((".git", "._"))` case-sensitive, `":Zone.Identifier" in name` a substring test), `:1689-1692` (extension filter), at `8c42799`
**Discovered:** 2026-11-04, product 3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c handoff (`L9B/task-18-report.md` :47-50, :67; `task-18-review.md` :23-24)

**Symptom:** the glob takes `.gvp` (gerbv project, x19), `.gpi` (EAGLE CAM log, x19), `.gtd` (GerbTool, x21), `.gbl` firmware (Miceuz EFR32, x12), `.gcode` / `.ngc` / `.g` G-code and `.g4` ANTLR grammars (atopile, x3). Each becomes an error record. Partly as filed: `.nc` is not matched by `*.g*`. It is a drill candidate (`:1683-1686`) and is taken only when its header reads as Excellon. `.GITIGNORE` on a case-insensitive checkout is read; `:Zone.Identifier` is matched anywhere in the name, not as a suffix.

**Fix direction / budget:** list Gerber extensions explicitly (or require a Gerber marker before recording an error for a non-layer extension); case-fold the dot-name test; `endswith(":Zone.Identifier")`. Output-changing: gerber `error` records / `layer_count` on those dirs.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The `*.g*` glob read gerbv projects, CAM logs and G-code as Gerber error records. Files without a layer extension now need a Gerber marker, dot-names are case-folded and Zone.Identifier is a suffix test. Files with a layer extension (`.gbl` firmware, `.g4` grammars) stay error records by ruling P5, as the issue's own fix direction allows.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 18211d8d (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `analyze_gerbers.py:1711-1738`: dot-names case-folded, `endswith(":Zone.Identifier")`; a `*.g*` file without a layer extension is read only when its first 8 KB hold `%FS`, `%MO` or a `G04...*` comment (`:1796`). Real output: festlv/thc drops `drill_0.8.g` and `drill_1.g` (G-code), 5 -> 3 layers.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-940: a power-typed split plane whose island has an auto-generated net name fails both power predicates


**Severity:** LOW (1 of 496 boards: +1 SU-001 error, score -12)
**File:** `skills/emc/scripts/emc_rules.py:1591-1606` (`_reference_plane_layers`: only zones whose net passes `_is_power_or_ground` count as plane fill), `:94-108` (`_is_power_or_ground`), at `8c42799`

## 2026-11-08 — KH-965: DFM ignores a market-inferred IPC Class 3 that `design_intent` reports; boolean `ipc_class` aliases Class 1


**Severity:** LOW (no corpus board resolves to Class 1 or 3; it surfaces only with a config)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/pcb/pipeline.py:460-471` (`_dfm_design_intent` returns None when `source.ipc_class == 'auto'`), `skills/kicad/scripts/design_intent.py:93` and `:283-295` (`True in {1, 2, 3}`; market fallback to 3), `skills/kicad/scripts/pcb/dfm.py:859` at `2abc8496`
**Discovered:** 2026-11-05, product 3.0.x Wave 10b handoff (new in Wave 10b; before it, DFM always ran Class 2)

**Symptom:** With config `{"design_intent": {"target_market": "medical"}}`, `resolve_design_intent` gives `ipc_class` 3 with source `auto`, but `_dfm_design_intent` returns None, so DFM judges against Class 2. Two blocks in one PCB output disagree. The boolean half is only partly confirmed. Through the CLI (`resolve_config`), `ipc_class: true` is caught by the `project_config` validator, which warns, deletes the key, and leaves Class 2. Only a caller that passes an unvalidated dict (`analyze_pcb(config=…)`, or `resolve_design_intent` directly) gets `ipc_class: True` with source `config`. DFM then accepts it as Class 1, because `True in (1, 2, 3)`.

**Fix direction / budget:** Decide whether a market-inferred class drives DFM. If not, have `design_intent` mark it as advisory so the two blocks agree. Reject `bool` in `design_intent.py:93` and `dfm.py:859`. Standard lane: 0 on the corpus (no `.kicad-happy.json`). Covered by a fixture test.

**Addendum 2026-11-06 (v3.0.2 Wave 11a, candidate `5510006a`, claimed fixed by the handoff; partly fixed):**
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 16b1d73d fix(pcb): a boolean ipc_class is not IPC Class 1 (v3.0.2 Wave 11a Task 10, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `5510006a`: the bool half landed: `design_intent.py:93` and `pcb/dfm.py:859` reject `bool`. The market half is only pinned by a test (`tools/tests/test_pcb_dfm.py:153` `test_market_class_does_not_drive_dfm`, which passes at the parent). There is no code change there.
- **Left open:** the two blocks still disagree. Probe: `{"design_intent": {"target_market": "medical"}}` → `design_intent.ipc_class` 3 (source `auto`), while DFM reports class 2 / `default` (`pcb/pipeline.py:471` unchanged). The filed fallback, marking the inferred class as advisory, was not done. If the maintainer counts "source: auto" as that mark, this is FIXED by decision, but no change landed.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** An inferred medical or aerospace market set `design_intent.ipc_class` to 3 while DFM judged Class 2. The market now only suggests Class 3 in the signals, so the two blocks agree; the boolean half was fixed in Wave 11a.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev c23ee07e (bool half 16b1d73d, Wave 11a) (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `design_intent.py:284-297`: the market branch no longer sets `ipc_class`; it adds an "IPC Class 3 suggested by ... (not applied ...)" signal. DFM still uses only config / fab-note / title-block classes (`pcb/pipeline.py:494-504`), so both blocks report class 2. Bool rejection at `design_intent.py:93`, `pcb/dfm.py:814`.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-966: op-amp SPICE bench reads a dead output (vdb ≈ −853 dB) as a gain error on below-minimum-supply benches


**Severity:** LOW (SP-WARN or info with a meaningless number and a misleading note)
**File:** `skills/spice/scripts/spice_results.py:289-323` (`evaluate_opamp_circuit`: no check for `gain_linear` 0 before the gain compare) and `:349-358` (below-minimum demotion); `skills/spice/scripts/spice_templates.py:589-591` (`vdb` measures) at `2abc8496`
**Discovered:** 2026-11-05, product 3.0.x Wave 10b handoff (pre-existing; the evaluator is unchanged at `e60d03b5` apart from the `vee_repaired` note)

**Symptom:** Partly confirmed. The stored corpus SPICE outputs, which predate Wave 10b, have 95 op-amp results in 28 units with `gain_error_dB` above 500: simulated `gain_dB` from −827 to −864, `gain_linear` 0.0, statuses 54 warn and 41 info. Example: amonbenson/expresso U7, NE5532 at 3.3 V supply, minimum 8 V. Every one of them is a below-minimum-supply bench with a behavioral model. The output node is dead, but the note says "may reflect testbench topology sensitivity or real GBW limitation". The 0.00 dB half does not hold. All 185 op-amp warn/fail results with `gain_error_dB` 0 carry a "supply N V below the part's minimum M V" note. The gain matches; the warn comes from the deliberate below-minimum demotion at `:349-358`.

**Fix direction / budget:** When `gain_linear` is 0, or vdb is below about −300 dB, report "output not driven (bench supply below the part's minimum)" with status info and no `gain_error_dB`. Lane: spice-offline, op-amp SP-WARN/info text and `delta` on about 28 units.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The op-amp evaluator compared a dead bench output (vdb near -853 dB) against the expected gain and called it a gain error; below -300 dB it now reports the output as not driven, with no gain comparison.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 21f27d74 (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `spice_results.py:236` `_DEAD_OUTPUT_DB = -300`; `:304-306` a gain below it gives status info, note 'Output not driven in the bench; no gain measured' and no `gain_error_dB` (the below-minimum supply note stays in `model_note`). A/B: 44 results / 14 units, 16 warn -> info.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-1034: VM-001 flags a switching regulator's own switch network as a domain crossing when its open-collector switch pins are judged at the current-sense resistor's rail (MC34063)


**Severity:** LOW (false error; one corpus unit seen, new with the open-collector-at-pull-up rule)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/validation_detectors.py:582-603` (open-collector pins judged at the pull-up rail), `:690-720` (pairing); `_is_regulator_like` `:528-539` does not know `MC34063`
**Discovered:** 2026-11-07, harness, v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 corpus gate (`results/v302_w11b1_gate`, standard lane)

**Symptom:** ice458/VFD-Clock `PCB/controler/controler.kicad_sch`: U1 `MC34063AP` (rescue symbol `…-rescue:MC34063AP-Regulator_Switching`) has `SwC` and `DC` (open_collector) and `Ipk` (input) on `__unnamed_0` with the Ipk sense resistor R1 to +5V. The candidate adds VM-001 error "Net __unnamed_0: 5.0V / 1.0V domain crossing without level shifter" (only U1 on the net; the 1.0 V side is a domain guess for U1's own input). The baseline had no such finding. The same pins are a regulator's switch network, which the budget removes VM-001 from elsewhere.

**Fix direction:** skip nets whose IC endpoints all belong to one part, and treat a part with a PR-DET regulator record (or `Regulator_Switching` symbol) as regulator-like.

---

- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `validation_detectors.py:694` and `:711` count distinct refs, not pins, so one part's own pins are never a crossing. Gate snap ice458/VFD-Clock controler: the '__unnamed_0: 5.0V / 1.0V' VM-001 is gone.

## 2026-11-08 — KH-1039: a symbol with a second `Value` property (a hidden empty copy from 2020–2021 Eagle imports) silently loses its value; no annotation says why


**Severity:** MEDIUM (whole BOMs read empty on the affected boards; downstream AU-DET / CD-DET / XL-DET lose findings and cross XV-002 reports schematic/PCB value mismatches, with nothing telling the user the cause)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/schematic/reader.py:421-429` `mandatory_property` (last duplicate wins, KH-711), `:751-768` `_symbol_fields`; annotation checks `skills/kicad/scripts/schematic/audits.py` (`annotation_issues`)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-07, harness, v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate (G2 adjudication); ruled 2026-11-07 by the user: keep the KiCad 10 reading, add an annotation

**Symptom:** Eagle-imported KiCad 6 files carry `(property "Value" "220" (id 1))` and a hidden `(property "Value" "" (id 4))` on the same symbol. Since KH-711 the last duplicate wins, as kicad-cli 10.0.8 reads it (`~`), so the part's value is empty. Gate census: 874 parts on 14 units went to an empty value (Arty100T sheets, BelaPlatform bela-hardware cape rev C1/C2/C3, CapableRobot capable_jetson_carrier `fpga.kicad_sch`). Corpus scan of the `.kicad_sch` sources: 65 files hold a symbol with two exact-name `Value` properties (299 symbols; on 146 the last copy is empty and the first is not), mostly format versions 20200506..20211123.

**Fix direction:** when a symbol has more than one property matching a mandatory field name, keep the KiCad 10 value but record it: an `annotation_issues` entry (e.g. `duplicate_value_field`, ref + the discarded text) and, when the kept copy is empty and an earlier one is not, a note that KiCad 10 shows no value while KiCad 6 showed the earlier one.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** Since KH-711 the last duplicate Value wins, as KiCad 10 reads it, so Eagle-imported symbols with a hidden empty second Value read empty with no explanation; the property audit now reports each such symbol with the shown and the ignored texts.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev f16661fb (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `6138b126`: `schematic/reader.py:1040-1044` keeps the earlier differing Value texts as `_dropped_values` when the shown value is the last copy's; `schematic/audits.py:1105-1120` adds one `duplicate_value_field` entry per reference to `property_issues` ('KiCad 10 reads the last and shows no value, ignoring ...'); popped at `presentation.py:57`. Gate candidate: 995 entries / 38 units (handoff ≈ 995 / 38).
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-2 whole-range gate `0f2deade..6138b126` vs `product_f53d107` (ledger `f53d107.json`), 2026-11-08: standard 149,633 units + full-chain 21,411, every moved unit claimed by the per-unit judge `regression/budgets/v302_wave11b2_judge.py` (0 residual); spice-offline, text oracle, `--schema`, distributor-offline and a gerber `--full` A/B as declared (records `results/v302_w11b2_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}/`).

## 2026-11-07 — KH-467: three LED forward-voltage tables disagree per colour — `audit_led_circuits` and `validate_led_resistors` assume different Vf for the same LED

**Severity:** LOW (both detectors are heuristic when no datasheet extraction is present; the disagreement means the two rules can reach different current estimates for one LED, and none of the three tables cites a source)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/domain_detectors.py:4815` (`_LED_VF`, nominal, read by `_estimate_led_vf` :4829 for `audit_led_circuits` :4848), `:4823` (`_LED_VF_FLOOR`, read at :5060); `skills/kicad/scripts/validation_detectors.py:1090` (`_LED_VF_BY_COLOR`, read by `_guess_led_color` :1099 and `validate_led_resistors` :1201)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-23, Checklist 11 (constants registry CONST-604 / CONST-605 / CONST-800, all unverified, critical-risk) at product `0490c49`

**Symptom:** the same colour maps to different forward voltages depending on which
rule evaluates the LED — nominal `_LED_VF` vs `_LED_VF_BY_COLOR`: red 2.0 vs 1.8,
yellow 2.0 vs 2.1, green 3.2 vs 2.2 (the floor table says 2.1), uv 3.5 vs 3.3;
`_LED_VF_BY_COLOR` carries `ir` (1.2) and the other two do not. Green is the
substantive one: 2.2 V is a GaP/AlGaInP green, 3.2 V an InGaN green, and the two
rules silently pick opposite technologies. Orange/amber agree.

**Measured 2026-10-23 (Checklist 11b, sources on CONST-604/605/800):** per-colour
typicals from the local LED datasheets (Würth 150060/150080 series, Kingbright APT2012,
Lite-On LTST-C170/C190/C191/C193, Vishay VLMO1300/VLMTG1500, Broadcom HSMW-C170, Cree
CLV1A-FKB, SunLED XZM2, OSRAM LY P47F) plus the Wikipedia LED material table:
red 1.95–2.1 (min 1.5–1.8), orange 2.0 (min 1.8), yellow 2.0–2.35 (min 1.95), amber 2.0,
blue 3.2–3.3 (min 2.5–2.8), white ~3.2 (min 2.7–2.9), UV 3.5–3.7 (min 3.1), IR 1.2–1.35.
**Green is genuinely bimodal:** GaP/AlInGaP green 2.0–2.2 V (LTST-C170GKT 2.1, VLMTG1500
2.0) vs InGaN green 3.2–3.3 V (150060GS 3.2, APT2012ZGCK 3.3, XZM2DG53W 3.2); the colour
word cannot pick one. So: `_LED_VF` 7/8 verified (green open); `_LED_VF_BY_COLOR` 6/9
(red 1.8 is the datasheet minimum, not the typical; green 2.2 is the other technology; UV
3.3 is below every sampled typical). **Floor rider:** `_LED_VF_FLOOR` red 1.85 / orange
2.0 / amber 2.0 / blue 3.0 / white 3.0 all sit ABOVE the sampled datasheet minimums, so
LA-004 can declare an LED dead on a rail it would light from (blue on 2.8 V); yellow /
green / UV floors verified. Corpus: 11,472 LEDs carry a colour hint (red 3,940, green
3,215, blue 1,311, ir 957, yellow 926, white 717, orange 223, amber 151, uv 32); 63,734
carry none and take the 2.0 V default in both detectors; LA-004 fired 5 times, all green.
For the unified table: nominal + minimum per colour as above, and for a bare "green" hint
either a 2.1/3.2 pair with the lower bound for LA-004 and the current estimate reported
as a range, or a technology keyword pass (`gap`, `ingan`, `pure green`, `true green`)
before falling back.

**Fix direction:** one shared table in `kicad_core` (the round-7 shared-tables
pattern) with a cited source per colour (manufacturer typical-Vf ranges, e.g.
Vishay / Kingbright / Würth colour tables), nominal + floor as two fields of one
entry; both detectors read it. Harness: register the table once and verify it under
Checklist 11b; the three current constants retire.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** Three LED forward-voltage tables disagreed by colour; one sourced table of nominal and floor voltages now serves LR-001, LA-AUD and LA-004.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 913404fe (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `kicad_core/parts.py:522-543` one `LED_VF_BY_COLOR` (nominal, floor) table read by every LED check.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate 2026-11-07 (baseline `5510006` = `727d0ab3` analyzer, candidate `f53d107e`, results/v302_w11b1_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}): standard 149,633 + full-chain 21,411 units, census exact, 0 candidate failures, 0 rc flips; every moved unit claimed by the merged budget under the per-unit judge (`regression/budgets/v302_wave11b1_judge.py`), 0 residual; spice-offline 160 / 8,830 reports differ, all on moved schematic units; `--schema` ×6 identical; text oracle exactly the 262 declared deltas; distributor-offline exactly the 7 declared files; tiers 3,656 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-468: `_ADC_RESOLUTION_MAP` — 15 of 29 part-number prefixes are wrong, span several resolutions, or name parts that do not exist

**Severity:** LOW (`detect_adc_circuits` reports `resolution_bits` from this table when no datasheet extraction is present; a wrong value mis-states the ADC in the report and feeds any LSB / noise-floor arithmetic downstream; no other detector reads it)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/domain_detectors.py:3068` (`_ADC_RESOLUTION_MAP`, read by `_infer_adc_resolution` :3082 — first substring match of `value + lib_id`, so a prefix stands for the whole family it names)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-23, Checklist 11b (constants registry CONST-553, critical-risk) at product `0490c49`; every entry checked against the manufacturer datasheet or product page (local `datasheets/` PDFs where held)

**Symptom:** 14 prefixes hold for their whole family and are now verified in the registry
(`ads111` 16, `ads101` 12, `ads131` 24, `ads868` 16, `mcp320` 12, `mcp346` 16, `mcp356` 24,
`max1161` 12, `max1198` 8, `adc081` 8, `adc082` 8, `adc121` 12, `adc122` 12, `nau780` 24).
The other 15 fall into three classes:

- **Wrong value** — `mcp330` 10 (MCP3301/02/04 are 13-bit; the 10-bit parts are MCP300x,
  which no prefix covers), `mcp355` 24 (MCP3550/51/53 are 22-bit), `max1192` 10 (MAX1192
  is a dual 8-bit), `ad770` 14 (AD7705..AD7709 are 16-bit, ADI AN-607).
- **One prefix, several resolutions** — `ads126` 24 (ADS1260/61 24-bit, ADS1262/63
  32-bit), `mcp342` 18 (MCP3421..24 18-bit, MCP3425..28 16-bit), `ltc24` 24 (LTC2440/2485
  24-bit, LTC2450..2483 16-bit), `ltc23` 16 (LTC2308/09 12, LTC2314/2320 14, LTC2310 16,
  LTC2372 18, LTC2376/78 20), `ad760` 16 (AD7605/06 16, AD7607 14, AD7608/09 18), `ad799` 8
  (AD7991 12, AD7995 10, AD7999 8), `max1163` 12 (MAX11632..37 12-bit, MAX11638/39 8-bit).
- **No such part at the manufacturer** — `ads861` (no ADS861x on ti.com; the 16-bit
  ADS8860/8861 do not contain this substring), `mcp340`, `max1194`, `max1141`.

Corpus exposure (42,307 schematic outputs): `ltc23` matches 8 repos and is wrong for 6
of them (LTC2372-18, LTC2376-20 ×2, LTC2378-20, LTC2310-16, LTC2309); `ads126` 3 repos,
all ADS1262 (32-bit reported as 24); `mcp355` 2 repos (MCP3550, 22 reported as 24); `mcp342`
13 repos, MCP3426/3428 (16-bit) in 4; `ltc24` 4 repos, LTC2451 (16-bit) in 1; `ad799` 1 repo
(AD7991, 12 reported as 8). The four nonexistent prefixes match nothing. A rider: the
substring match also fires on passives whose `lib_id` embeds the board name
(`ADS1262…:C` capacitors) — harmless today because only ADC candidates reach the lookup.

**Fix direction:** key the table on full part-number stems long enough to be
resolution-unique (`ads1262`, `ads1261`, `mcp3421`..`mcp3428`, `ltc2440`, `ltc2309`,
`ltc2372`, `ad7606`, `ad7607`, `ad7991`, …), correct the four wrong values, drop the four
dead prefixes, and cite the datasheet per row (shared-table pattern, like KH-467). Where a
family genuinely splits (LTC23xx), return `None` rather than a guess. Harness: re-register
and verify under Checklist 11b after the fix; the corpus units above change
`resolution_bits` and are the gate budget.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The ADC resolution map used short prefixes that were wrong, ambiguous or named nonexistent parts; it is keyed on resolution-unique stems matched longest first. Two stems still overreach (`max1161` gives 12 bits to the 10-bit MAX11610/11, `ad7606` gives 16 to AD7606C-18), filed separately.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev cf604bfb (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `domain_detectors.py:3054-3076`: every correction and drop from the issue present; LTC23xx `-NN` suffix read as bits.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-476: `_KNOWN_FREQS` keys name one member of a multi-part datasheet, so the siblings fall to the 500 kHz topology default

**Severity:** LOW (`detect_power_regulators` reports `switching_frequency_hz` / `freq_source: topology_default` for the sibling parts; EMC rules and `cross_analysis` then size harmonic reach from 500 kHz instead of the datasheet 2.25 MHz / 1.5 MHz; no reference assertion involved)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/kicad_core/parts.py:208` (`_KNOWN_FREQS`, read by `lookup_switching_freq` :327 — longest `startswith` prefix, so a key only covers the part numbers that begin with it)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-24, Checklist 11b (constants registry CONST-835, the three unverified entries) at product `a0df172`; the two TI entries were checked against the local datasheets

**Symptom:** the values are right but the keys are too narrow for their own datasheets:

- `'TPS62160': 2.25e6` — TI SLVSAM2E covers TPS62160/62161/62162/62163 at one nominal 2.25 MHz; corpus designs carry TPS62162 and TPS62163 (11 regulator findings) and every one is reported at 500 kHz `topology_default`.
- `'TPS63000': 1.5e6` — TI SLVS520C covers TPS63000/63001/63002 with one oscillator row (1250 min / 1500 max kHz); TPS63001/63002 (20 regulator findings) default to 500 kHz. The product's own `_REGULATOR_VREF` (parts.py:31) keys the same family as `'TPS6300'`, so the two tables disagree on who is in the family.

Together 31 findings whose part values appear on 37 units / 20 repos. A corpus scan of every `topology_default` switching regulator whose value begins with a table key minus its last one or two characters lists 259 findings on 222 units across 30 keys (TPS61023/TPS61235/TPS54202/TPS54331/TPS61391/TPS61170/TPS61090 lead); those are candidates only — most are different families with different frequencies (TPS6104x, TPS6120x, TPS54335) and need their own datasheet before any key is widened. The two above are the ones the datasheets settle.

**Expected:** key the table by the datasheet family where the family shares one frequency (`'TPS6216'`, `'TPS6300'`), as KH-237 did for the sub-family splits, and keep `_REGULATOR_VREF` and `_KNOWN_FREQS` on the same family keys. The 4-digit-suffix siblings (`TPS62160-Q1`, `TPS63001DRCR`) then resolve by the same prefix.

**Harness:** CONST-835 entries TPS62160 / TPS63000 verified with these notes; near-miss scan not kept (one-shot).

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The switching-frequency keys named single family members, so TPS62161-63 and TPS63001/02 fell to the 500 kHz default; the keys are now the family prefixes.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev cf604bfb (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `kicad_core/parts.py:347` `TPS6216` 2.25 MHz, `:404` `TPS6300` 1.5 MHz; longest-prefix lookup `:453-455`.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate 2026-11-07 (baseline `5510006` = `727d0ab3` analyzer, candidate `f53d107e`, results/v302_w11b1_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}): standard 149,633 + full-chain 21,411 units, census exact, 0 candidate failures, 0 rc flips; every moved unit claimed by the merged budget under the per-unit judge (`regression/budgets/v302_wave11b1_judge.py`), 0 residual; spice-offline 160 / 8,830 reports differ, all on moved schematic units; `--schema` ×6 identical; text oracle exactly the 262 declared deltas; distributor-offline exactly the 7 declared files; tiers 3,656 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-482: truncated or non-KiCad input parses as a partial tree or one bare atom — exit 0, `diagnostics: []`

**Severity:** LOW (malformed input; the empty / whitespace-only case is now a usage error since `c6f4807`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/kicad_core/sexp.py:91-96` (raises only when `pos >= len(tokens)` at entry; the list loop `while pos < len(tokens) and tokens[pos] != ")"` exits silently at EOF); `kicad_core/project.py:376-385` rejects whitespace-only files only
**Discovered:** 2026-10-24, v3 round-9b handoff §7 item 3 (review A-I4); reproduced at `07b7fb1` — a fixture cut at 3,000 of 4,220 bytes and a plain-text file both exit 0 with `diagnostics: []` (the text file gives `components: 0`, `kicad_version: "unknown"`); `analyze_pcb` likewise exits 0 with 0 footprints

**Fix direction:** record one `diagnostics` entry when the parser reaches EOF inside an open list (truncation) or when the root atom is not `kicad_sch` / `kicad_pcb` (garbage). The maintainer removed a root-token REJECTION under ruling R14 because dozens of gate units with non-standard roots would have become rc 2 — so this must be a diagnostic, not an exit code. Budget: `envelope/diagnostics` on those non-standard-root units (size: count corpus units whose root atom is not the canonical one before choosing the wording).

#### Addendum to KH-482 (truncated / non-KiCad input)
**Added:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` part a, Empirical: "R1: deep nesting refusal")
`kicad_core/sexp.py` `parse` is recursive. Nesting depth 990 parses, and depth 1100 raises `RecursionError` with a traceback and no diagnostic. Only adversarial input reaches it. Fold it into the same diagnostic: an iterative parser, or catch and record.

**Addendum 2026-11-06 (v3.0.2 Wave 11a, candidate `5510006a`, partly fixed):**
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev d0a5de36 test: S-expression parser properties over truncated and mutated KiCad files (v3.0.2 Wave 11a Task 2, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `5510006a`: tests only (`tools/tests/test_sexp_properties.py`). `kicad_core/sexp.py` is unchanged in this behaviour (its only touch is b3bbcfbe, `unescape_quoted`). Probe: `parse('(kicad_sch (a 1) (b')` still returns a partial tree silently, and depth 1100 still raises RecursionError.
- **Left open:** the diagnostic for truncated or non-KiCad input and the deep-nesting case are planned for 11b (expected PARTIAL).

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The S-expression parser stopped silently at a truncated end of file and recursed without a limit; it is now iterative, reports truncation and nesting deeper than 200, and the pipelines record a diagnostic for a truncated file or a non-KiCad root (exit code unchanged).
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 3dc0c69f (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `kicad_core/sexp.py:104` `parse_checked`, truncation `:243`, `_MAX_NESTING = 200` `:223`; `project.py:571` root-type check; wired into the schematic root, sub-sheets and the board.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-529: `power_sequencing` PG→EN edges exist only when the consumer regulator precedes the producer in `power_regulators` [group 8]

**Severity:** MEDIUM (multi-regulator designs with PG→EN chains; order-dependent)
**File:** `schematic/system_analyses.py:1644-1647` (`analyze_power_sequencing`: the PG scan runs inside the per-regulator loop over the `dependencies` appended so far; no post-loop join)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R4-F7)

**Symptom:** regulator A's PG drives regulator B's EN; when B is listed before A the edge is recorded, when after it is lost. No ordering contract exists.

**Fix direction / budget:** two passes, build all dependencies, then join PG→EN. Budget: small; `power_sequencing` edges / `sequence_order` on multi-regulator units. The meaning of `sequence_order` (startup dependency vs PG→EN depth) is an open ruling but does not block this fix.

**Note 2026-10-25 (product 3.0.x Wave 2):** not part of Wave 2; REPORT-4 A4-F7 (PG -> EN sequencing) stays with the system-analyses group.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The PG -> EN link was searched inside the per-regulator loop over the dependencies built so far; it now runs after all are built, so the edge no longer depends on list order.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev b53ceffe (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `schematic/system_analyses.py:1772-1779`: the PG -> EN join runs after all regulator dependencies are built.

**Severity:** MEDIUM (small population; VD-001 / VD-004)
**File:** `schematic/system_analyses.py:749-755` (selection), `:807-818` in `analyze_voltage_derating` (`_find_power_net` takes the pin-1 power net, ignores the other terminal unless ground; `v_rail <= 0` skips negative outputs, which `signal_detectors.py:1961` produces by negating inverting Vout)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R4-F6)

**Symptom:** a cap between +12V and +5V is derated against 12 V (stress is |V1 − V2| = 7 V); a cap on −12V is skipped. Negative rails named `-12V` also depend on the sign fix (KH-519).

**Fix direction / budget:** stress = |V(pin1) − V(pin2)| with ground = 0 and signed rails. Budget: VD-001 / VD-004 movement on rail-to-rail and negative-rail caps; land after KH-519.

---

## 2026-11-07 — KH-533: FS-001 "requires external compensation" lists internally compensated parts (LM2596/LM2576, LM317/337/350, TPS5430/5450, MC3406x) and prescribes a harmful 10 nF FB→GND cap [group 9]

**Severity:** HIGH (every LM2596-ADJ / LM317 board with an empty FB net; the suggested fix can hurt the loop)
**File:** `validation_detectors.py:1325-1332` (`_REQUIRES_COMPENSATION_KEYWORDS`), `:1406-1429` (`validate_feedback_stability`, warning + `fix_params`); `:1380` ("divider impedance too low" info)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R7-F7)

**Symptom:** LM2596/LM2576 (Simple Switcher) and TPS5430/5450 are internally compensated; LM317/337/350 and LT108x ADJ bypass caps are optional ripple-rejection parts; MC3406x has no compensation pin. Only UC384x/UC282x COMP and TPS40xxx controllers need an external network. The fix prescribes 10 nF FB→GND, which adds a pole on a FB node. The low-impedance info also fires on the LM317 datasheet-standard 240 Ω / 720 Ω divider (180 Ω parallel, needed for the minimum load current).

**Fix direction / budget:** reduce the keyword list to parts that really need external compensation (UC384x / UC282x / TPS40xxx), drop the FB→GND prescription, exempt LM317-class dividers from the low-impedance info. Budget: FS-001 disappearances on LM2596 / LM317 / TPS54xx units (size first) plus the info disappearances.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** The external-compensation list named internally compensated parts and prescribed a 10 nF cap; only parts with a compensation pin remain, the prescription is gone, and an LM2596/LM2576 divider inside its data sheet's R1 range is not too low.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 9012493b (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `validation_detectors.py:1440-1443` list reduced to 4; the 10 nF `fix_params` removed; R1-range exemption `:1465`, `:1504-1506` (LM2596 240 ohm-1.5 kohm, LM2576 1-5 kohm, checked against 4 local data sheets each).
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate 2026-11-07 (baseline `5510006` = `727d0ab3` analyzer, candidate `f53d107e`, results/v302_w11b1_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}): standard 149,633 + full-chain 21,411 units, census exact, 0 candidate failures, 0 rc flips; every moved unit claimed by the merged budget under the per-unit judge (`regression/budgets/v302_wave11b1_judge.py`), 0 residual; spice-offline 160 / 8,830 reports differ, all on moved schematic units; `--schema` ×6 identical; text oracle exactly the 262 declared deltas; distributor-offline exactly the 7 declared files; tiers 3,656 / 0 / 8 / 4.

**File:** `kicad_core/project.py:183-209` (`is_referenced_as_child` / `_root_references_target`: substring membership of rel path or basename, child Sheetfile references never followed), `:264-286` (`discover_root_schematic` tier 3)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R1-F7)

**Symptom:** invoking the analyzer on a grandchild sheet in a nested directory finds no root, so the leaf is analysed alone (with a warning pointing to `--project-root`, `schematic/pipeline.py:1264-1270`). A sheet named `adc.kicad_sch` is wrongly found as referenced by a root that contains `my_adc.kicad_sch`.

**Fix direction / budget:** parse `Sheetfile` properties and walk the hierarchy; compare whole path components. Budget: ≈0 (the corpus runs roots); leaf invocations only.

**Addendum 2026-11-06 (v3.0.2 Wave 11a, candidate `5510006a`, partly fixed):**
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 4a63e3e2 fix(schematic): root discovery follows whole sheet-file paths through intermediate sheets (v3.0.2 Wave 11a Task 31, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `5510006a`: `_root_references_target` walks the hierarchy over whole-path `Sheetfile` refs (`skills/kicad/scripts/kicad_core/project.py:351-390`). Tier 2 of `discover_root_schematic` also compares whole paths (`:452`). Probes:
  - a grandchild `a/b/leaf.kicad_sch` finds `root.kicad_sch`;
  - `adc.kicad_sch` is no longer matched by a root naming `my_adc.kicad_sch` (returns None).
- **Left open:** `is_referenced_as_child` (`project.py:314-342`, used by `detect_sub_sheet`) still tests `basename in content`. Probe: `is_referenced_as_child('x/adc.kicad_sch')` gives True when the sibling names only `my_adc.kicad_sch`. This is the sub-sheet half, planned for 11b (expected PARTIAL).

---

- **Root cause / fix:** Sub-sheet detection tested whether a sibling file's text contained the basename; it now compares whole resolved Sheetfile paths, so `adc` no longer matches `my_adc`.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 07ce40df (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `kicad_core/project.py:300-336` `is_referenced_as_child` compares whole Sheetfile paths with text variables expanded; the `basename in content` test is gone (the root-discovery half shipped in Wave 11a, `4a63e3e2`).
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate 2026-11-07 (baseline `5510006` = `727d0ab3` analyzer, candidate `f53d107e`, results/v302_w11b1_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}): standard 149,633 + full-chain 21,411 units, census exact, 0 candidate failures, 0 rc flips; every moved unit claimed by the merged budget under the per-unit judge (`regression/budgets/v302_wave11b1_judge.py`), 0 residual; spice-offline 160 / 8,830 reports differ, all on moved schematic units; `--schema` ×6 identical; text oracle exactly the 262 declared deltas; distributor-offline exactly the 7 declared files; tiers 3,656 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-647: DNS rebinding between the download URL check and the connect

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**File:** `skills/datasheets/distributor_core/download.py:100` (`_resolve`), `:112` (`_address_problem`), `:350` (`download_pdf`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, recorded as residue by the product 3.0.x Wave 1 security round (`63f6a20`)

**Symptom:** `url_problem` resolves the host and requires every address to be public, then requests/urllib resolve the name again when they connect. A server that answers the check with a public address and the connect with a private one (short TTL) passes the policy.

**Fix direction / budget:** connect to the address that was checked (pin the resolved IP, keep the Host header / SNI), on every redirect hop. Budget: output-neutral; the distributor-offline oracle replays recorded URLs, re-check both ways.

**Addendum 2026-11-06 (v3.0.2 Wave 11a, candidate `5510006a`, claimed fixed by the handoff; partly fixed):**
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 98d853ba fix(datasheets): connect each download to the address the URL check approved; b34bee4a fix(datasheets): keep requests first and pin it to the checked address; 98f35457 fix(datasheets): try each resolved address once…; 68e63cc1 fix(datasheets): refuse IPv6 addresses that embed a private IPv4 address (v3.0.2 Wave 11a Task 7, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `5510006a`:
  - urllib connects only to the checked addresses through `_pinned_create_connection`, keeping the host for SNI and the certificate (`skills/datasheets/distributor_core/download.py:285-299`). Every redirect is re-pinned (`:278-282`).
  - requests ≥2.32.2 goes through `_PinnedAdapter` (`:651-695`).
- **Left open:**
  - (a) With requests older than 2.32.2, `_PinnedAdapter` is None, yet `download_pdf` still tries requests first, unpinned (`:463-465`, comment `:643`). Ruling 24 said to skip the requests transport under the default policy; the commit kept it first instead.
  - (b) The Playwright fallback checks `url_problem` and then lets `route.fetch` resolve the name again (`:820-822`). A server that answers the first two methods with a non-PDF reaches the fallback, where the rebinding window is still open.
  - Both are documented in `.github/SECURITY.md:32` ("the host is resolved again"). Proxies are unpinned by design.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** Requests older than 2.32.2 and the browser fallback resolved the host again after the address check; under the default policy neither is used, so every download connects to the checked address.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev 9eab79e5 (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `distributor_core/download.py:466-470`, `_requests_usable` `:546`, `:823`; `.github/SECURITY.md`; product `test_download_policy` 52 run / 0 fail on requests 2.31.0 (`OldRequestsTest` runs), Playwright 1.48.0 + 1.64.1 `RealPlaywrightTest` + `PlaywrightRouteTest` 9/9 each.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate 2026-11-07 (baseline `5510006` = `727d0ab3` analyzer, candidate `f53d107e`, results/v302_w11b1_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}): standard 149,633 + full-chain 21,411 units, census exact, 0 candidate failures, 0 rc flips; every moved unit claimed by the merged budget under the per-unit judge (`regression/budgets/v302_wave11b1_judge.py`), 0 residual; spice-offline 160 / 8,830 reports differ, all on moved schematic units; `--schema` ×6 identical; text oracle exactly the 262 declared deltas; distributor-offline exactly the 7 declared files; tiers 3,656 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-653: `PH0` / `PH1` GPIO pins read as a regulator SW pin, so STM32s become `ic_with_internal_regulator` / switching regulator records

**Severity:** MEDIUM (false regulator records with inductor, rail, RS-001 / DO-DET / PS-001 and downstream EMC / thermal / cross consequences on common MCUs)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/signal_detectors.py:1618` (`pn_base = pname.rstrip("0123456789").rstrip("_")`), `:1627` (`pn_parts & {"SW", "PH", "LX"}`), `:1839` (same token list)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, product 3.0.x Wave 2 (`004bba5`, handoff §Asks 4a); verified in source at `004bba5`

**Symptom:** stripping trailing digits turns the GPIO pins `PH0` / `PH1` (STM32 port H, usually the HSE oscillator pins) into `PH`, a TI SW-pin alias, so the MCU is taken for a switching regulator and the inductor search runs over its oscillator nets. Examples at the Wave 2 gate: cansat / Cubesat-EPS U4 (STM32F405, rail `3.3V_STM`), BerkeleyLab/Marble U54 (STM32F207, KH-421), bluerobotics ping-dev-kit U301 (STM32H563), formulaslug U1 (STM32WB55). Wave 2 made the pick deterministic (KH-509); the misread itself stays: most of the 51 H1 schematic units / 39 repos at the gate are these records.

**Fix direction / budget:** match `PH` only as the exact pin name (or `PH` + non-port suffix), never after digit stripping; or require the part to be a regulator family before the SW-pin aliases count. Budget: PR-DET / DO-DET / PS-001 / RS-001 records disappear on MCU refs plus downstream EMC / thermal / cross on those units; size with a corpus count of PR-DET records whose SW pin name matches `^PH\d`.

---

- **Root cause / fix:** Stripping trailing digits turned the MCU GPIOs PH0/PH1 into the switch-pin alias `PH`; a PHn pin now keeps its full name when the part also has GPIO pins on another port.
- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev a459f394 (v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).
- **Verification:** harness re-read at `f53d107e`: `signal_detectors.py:1688` `_GPIO_PORT_PIN ^P[A-GI-K]\d{1,2}$`; `:1733-1738` keeps the full PHn name.
- **Gate:** v3.0.2 Wave 11b-1 gate 2026-11-07 (baseline `5510006` = `727d0ab3` analyzer, candidate `f53d107e`, results/v302_w11b1_gate{,_fc,_aux,_do}): standard 149,633 + full-chain 21,411 units, census exact, 0 candidate failures, 0 rc flips; every moved unit claimed by the merged budget under the per-unit judge (`regression/budgets/v302_wave11b1_judge.py`), 0 residual; spice-offline 160 / 8,830 reports differ, all on moved schematic units; `--schema` ×6 identical; text oracle exactly the 262 declared deltas; distributor-offline exactly the 7 declared files; tiers 3,656 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-07 — KH-671: a root-sheet hierarchical label is keyed by its bare name and fuses with a global label or global bus member of the same name

**Severity:** MEDIUM
