## 2026-11-04 — KH-443: Net ties are not bridged by the DC-continuity audits — RS-001 false "no declared source" when a rail is fed through a `NetTie_2`; PP-001 / power tracing have the same blind spot (GitHub #50)


**Severity:** MEDIUM (false RS-001 WARNING on a rail that is sourced; corpus:
213 `.kicad_sch` files / 136 repos place `Device:NetTie_*`, 565 `.kicad_pcb`
files carry `net_tie_pad_groups`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/signal_detectors.py` — `audit_rail_sources`
(RS-001/002, bridges `solder_jumpers` with `default_state == "bridged"` only),
`audit_power_pin_dc_paths` (PP-001 `_bridges_dc`: inductor / ferrite / fuse /
≤1 Ω resistor / bridged jumper — no `net_tie`); any other consumer that walks
DC continuity (power_budget rail attribution, regulator output→rail mapping)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-14, GitHub #50 (bson): "Net ties aren't understood…
can be treated as 0R resistor arrays… but of course there is no BOM part"
**Reported by:** bson (GitHub #50)

**Repro (verified 2026-10-14 at main `0684046`, kicad-cli 10.0.6 oracle):**
`repos/Envious-Data/EnvOpenPico/RP2040/EnvPicoLiPo/EnvPicoLiPo.kicad_sch` —
U1 BQ24072RGT pin 10 `OUT` (`power_out`) sits on `Net-(C2-Pad2)` (analyzer
`__unnamed_8`); NT1 `Device:NetTie_2` pin 1 is on that net, pin 2 on `VDD`,
which carries U2 `Vin` (`power_in`), C3, R4. kicad-cli keeps the two nets
distinct (correct — a net tie IS two nets in KiCad) and the analyzer's net
membership matches the oracle exactly. But `audit_rail_sources` emits
**RS-001 "VDD has no declared source"** (description: "…no bridged solder
jumper path to a sourced net") although the rail is sourced one net-tie hop
away. The same audit would have accepted a bridged `SolderJumper` in NT1's
place. Pattern example (no RS-001 fires there today — the rails carry
`#PWR` symbols): `greatscottgadgets/hackrf/hardware/hackrf-one` NT2 ties
`REG_OUT1`↔`VCC` and NT1 `REG_OUT2`↔`+1V8`, so U21 TPS62410's outputs reach
their rails only through ties; regulator→rail attribution (power_budget,
DC-001 output-cap checks) cannot cross them either.
Counter-evidence checked: `piotr-binkowski/kintex-pcie-board` NT6/NT3 tie
`MGTAVCC`/`+1V8` to U8 `FB3`/`FB1` (feedback sense) — the PP-001 fires there
are NOT tie-caused (U8 VOUT3 is on `MGTAVCC` directly).

**What already works (so #50's "not identified" is only half right):**
`kicad_utils` classifies `NT*` refs / `NetTie` lib_ids / values as
`type: "net_tie"`; `in_bom no` is honoured, so NTs never enter
`missing_mpn`, SS-001 or `bom_coverage`; SP-001 excludes them; the
datasheet-sync scripts and `lifecycle_audit` skip them; `analyze_pcb`
exports `net_tie_pad_groups` per footprint.

**Minor rider:** `simulation_readiness.components_without_model` lists
every NT (868-antenna: NT1..NT4; EnvPicoLiPo: NT1) — a net tie needs no
SPICE model; exempt `net_tie` (and arguably `jumper`) in that filter at
`analyze_schematic.py` ≈ l.6040.

**Fix direction:** treat `type == "net_tie"` as an always-bridged jumper in
`audit_rail_sources` and `_bridges_dc` (one predicate shared by both — the
PR #44 fuse-bridge change is the template), keep net membership untouched
(KiCad ground truth), and record the hop in the RS finding the way
`source_path: "bridged_jumper"` does (`"net_tie"`). Gate budget: RS-001
disappearances + RS-00x info "sourced via net tie" appearances on the ≈136
NetTie repos; PP-001 disappearances where the only rail path crosses a tie;
`components_without_model` shrinks by the NT count. Not for the PCB side:
`net_tie_pad_groups` already lets copper join the two nets; no analyzer rule
flags that join today.

#### Addendum to KH-443 (net ties not bridged)
**Added:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R5-F11)
RS-003 traversal has the same scope question. The comment at `skills/kicad/scripts/signal_detectors.py:4311-4312` and SKILL.md say it crosses a "bridged jumper / ferrite", but `:4244` iterates only `bridge_facts.jumpers`. Ruling needed together with this item: should RS-003 (and the bridge set generally) traverse ferrites, fuses and 0 Ω parts, or jumpers only? Then align the code or the comment.

- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `3642bcf3` (9b T6) (3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff): net ties are one conductor in RS-001 / PP-001.
- **Verification:** product 3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c gate (`389fbd5` → `8c42799`, results/v301_w9bc_gate). Std gate: RS-001 −97 / +14 and PP-001 −2,041 / +17 across the schematic lane, all on units the budget labels (no residual); harness fixture `tests/fixtures/net_tie/` (`tests/test_net_tie_rail_source.py`) RS-001 on the tied rail at `389fbd5`, none at `8c42799`; `NT?` duplicate references join nothing (locked by the same test). Rider (simulation readiness lists net ties as components without a model) filed separately as KH-916. GitHub #50 gets the product reply at release.

## 2026-11-04 — KH-796: the switching-loop area is a centre-triangle proxy, not the hot loop


**Severity:** LOW
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/pcb/assembly.py` (switching-loop estimate), `kicad_core/hotloop.py`; `skills/emc/scripts/emc_rules.py` (SW-003)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-31, product 3.0.x Wave 5 handoff follow-up 7 (GitHub #62 follow-up; KH-790 remainder); not verified harness-side

**Symptom:** the area is a shoelace over cap / IC / inductor centres. A buck hot loop is Cin → VIN → GND → Cin GND (the inductor is not in it); a boost loop is switch → diode/FET → Cout. Long near-lines just over 1 mm² still read as small loops (BlueJayRacing IC6: 1.2 mm² over 48 mm).

**Fix direction / budget:** a topology-aware loop from pads and tracks. Budget: full-chain SW-003 and `switching_loop_areas` (standard PCB outputs carry none: no `--schematic` in that profile).

- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `48bc7296`, `4660efe0` (9b T19); SW-003 grading `d6eed6f7`, `a2b05b83` (9c T9) (3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff): the hot loop is measured pad to pad through the nearest input cap (`method: "pad"`, `loop_pads`, 6 vertices); SW-003 grades only pad loops and reports a centre triangle as an ungraded info estimate.
- **Verification:** product 3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c gate (`389fbd5` → `8c42799`, results/v301_w9bc_gate). No corpus lane passes `--schematic`, so the pad path is gate-blind (KH-931); verified by the harness fixture `tests/fixtures/hotloop/buck.kicad_pcb` (`tests/test_hotloop_pad_fixture.py`: 120.0 mm² pad loop, SW-003 error from the pad loop, 35 mm² centre triangle → info "not graded") and the rewritten `tests/test_switching_loop.py`; product targeted check on 100 boards, 30/30 areas equal to the KiCad IPC-D-356 oracle. Std gate EMC: 447 SW-003 rewritten in place (≈440 estimated). GitHub #62 gets the product reply at release. Open follow-ups: KH-930, KH-931.

## 2026-11-04 — KH-894: supply-rail recognition is by net name only, so a rail whose KiCad name is not rail-like loses its decoupling group and gains RC filters (su-pcb SPICE benches flip decoupling → rc_filter)


**Severity:** LOW (decoupling / RC-DET / SPICE bench type on supply nets with non-rail names)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/kicad_core/netnames.py:111` (`is_power_net_name`); consumers `skills/kicad/scripts/signal_detectors.py:1245` (`detect_decoupling`, per power rail) and `:523` (`detect_rc_filters` needs a shared SIGNAL net, so a non-rail supply qualifies)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-03, harness Wave 8c + 8b gate spice-offline lane (product asked for a "component order" KH; measured cause is the net name); verified harness-side at `0efc012`: `is_power_net_name` True for `CAN_VCC`, `VCC_PROTECTED`, `3V3_PROTECTED`, `VBUS_PROT`, False for `CAN_VCC_PROTECTED` and `lclprotecteddvc1`

**Symptom:** KH-800 gives two su-pcb nets their KiCad names with unchanged pins: `EQM-SU-PCB` `/…9b57…/CAN_VCC` → `/…d779…/CAN_VCC_PROTECTED` (IC5.3, IC13.3, C3/C4/C50/C51, R193, R87) and `SU-PCB-OLD` `/…fe149/MEM_VCC` → `/…c945/lclprotecteddvc1`. Under the new names the nets are no longer rails: the decoupling group (C4, C51, C3, C50) disappears, RC-DET pairs R193/C3 and R87/C3 with the supply as output (2 and 4 filters), and the SPICE benches change type (decoupling −1, rc_filter +2 / +4). Connectivity is identical; only the name decides. The analyzer had the same blind spot for any design that names a supply this way (it was hidden here by the old tie-break picking a rail-like name).

**Fix direction / budget:** treat a net as a rail from its pins as well as its name (a net feeding `power_in` supply pins of ICs, or carrying a power symbol on another sheet), and/or widen the name rule to `<prefix>_VCC_<suffix>`; RC-DET should not take a net that feeds IC supply pins as a filter output. Output-changing: decoupling / RC-DET / PP-001 and SPICE benches; measure before budgeting. Same family as KH-877. Post-3.0.

- **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `ad5629e0`, `8564354c` (9b T8) (3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff): a net whose pins make it a supply (passive VCC pin with caps to ground) is a power rail; bridge / motor-driver outputs are not.
- **Verification:** product 3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c gate (`389fbd5` → `8c42799`, results/v301_w9bc_gate). Std gate: su-pcb `EQM-SU-PCB.kicad_sch` now has "Decoupling on …/CAN_VCC_PROTECTED" and loses 6 RC-DET (MCU sheet: "Decoupling on CAN_VCC"); harness fixture `tests/fixtures/topology_rail/` (`tests/test_topology_rail.py`) red at `389fbd5`, green at `8c42799`, with an `OSC_IN` crystal net as the negative control.

## 2026-11-04 — KH-895: TE-001 counts `TP`-prefixed capacitive touch pads as test points — test-point recognition is by reference prefix


**Severity:** LOW (test-coverage count and TE-001 text on boards that name touch electrodes `TP<n>`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/pcb/assembly.py` — `07b7fb1` :800 / :832 (inline `ref.upper().startswith("TP")`); `5687ee1` :814 `_is_test_point` (prefix OR `pad_prop_testpoint`; the prefix alone still admits the pad). **Discovered:** 2026-11-03, SacMap rev2 soak run 10 (`~/Projects/sandbox/Old-Reviews/sacmap-rev2/10/`, product `07b7fb1` = v3.0.0 release base; `REVIEW-2026-11-03.md` / `-meta.md`); verified harness-side by code read at `07b7fb1` and v3.0.x-dev `5687ee1`

**Symptom:** SacMap touch pads (value `TouchPad`, footprint `sacmap:Touch`, reference `TP<n>`) are counted in `test_point_count` and as net coverage for TE-001. PCB half of KH-436 (schematic `test_coverage`, with its FD-001 rider); fix together from the CP-003 touch-pad classifier.

**Fix direction / budget:** exclude a `TP` reference whose value or footprint names a touch / capacitive sensor (`touch`, `cap_sense`, `electrode`), or require a test-point footprint / pad property when the value contradicts it. - **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `efad984d` (9b T13) (3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff): capacitive touch pads with TP references are not test points (PCB TE-001 and schematic `test_coverage`).
- **Verification:** product 3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c gate (`389fbd5` → `8c42799`, results/v301_w9bc_gate). Std gate PCB lane: TE-001 rewritten in place on 2 boards (counts unchanged), labelled; the product A/B gave meiji-led-ring 13 → 5 TPs, plan44 5 → 1, SacMap 2 → 0. KH-436 keeps its FD-001 rider.

## 2026-11-04 — KH-920: load switches and USB power switches were recorded as LDO regulators

**Severity:** LOW
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/signal_detectors.py` (`_screen_regulator_candidate`, `audit_rail_sources`); `skills/kicad/scripts/kicad_core/parts.py` (`LOAD_SWITCH_KEYWORDS`); `skills/kicad/scripts/domain_detectors.py` (`detect_power_path`)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-04, product 3.0.x Waves 9b + 9c handoff (`L9B/task-9-report.md`); filed FIXED-direct. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `9bf13f0b` + `40c6d163` (3.0.x Wave 9b, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** the regulator screen excluded only its own short power-mux list. Load / USB power switches (MT9700, SY6280, AP2171/AP2191, TPS206x, STMPS2, NCP380, …) were typed LDO, and a phantom PR-DET record gave them an `output_rail`, DO-DET "regulator missing capacitors" and PS-001 "PG status unknown". The load-switch keyword list lived privately in `domain_detectors`.
- **Fix:** `9bf13f0b` moves the list to a shared `LOAD_SWITCH_KEYWORDS` in `kicad_core/parts.py` (adding `tps206`, `ap217`, `mt9700`, `sy628`), used by both the regulator screen (`signal_detectors.py:1763` at `8c42799`) and `detect_power_path` (`domain_detectors.py:2810`). `40c6d163` makes `audit_rail_sources` treat a switch's output net as sourced when its input conductor is sourced (fixpoint over chains, `signal_detectors.py:4396-4497`), so removing the phantom regulator does not leave its output as an unsourced rail.
- **Verification:** product A/B on the 52 census roots carrying these parts, base `8564354` vs `40c6d163`: PR-DET -72, DO-DET -12, PS-001 -3, PP-DET +27 (true `load_switch` detections), RS-001 +13. The 13 are switch outputs whose input rail is itself unsourced and already carries an RS-001 in the same file. The same-file restatement was hand-checked 13/13. Old-gap set (215 roots with a PP-DET load switch, `9bf13f0` vs `40c6d163`): RS-001 -35, 0 added. sample300: PR-DET -26, PP-DET +6, DO-DET -1, RS-001 -2. Full chain (28 roots): EMC and cross_analysis 0/28 moved, thermal `skipped_components` / summary only. Product tests 2,367 OK; harness unit 2,872 passed / 1 xfailed, contract 685 / 8 skipped / 3 xfailed. Determinism PYTHONHASHSEED 0 vs 1 identical on 12 roots. Net-tie sample 0 deltas.
- **Residual (filed open as KH-946):** `audit_rail_sources` pairs every input net with every output net of a switch (`signal_detectors.py:4477-4487` at `8c42799`), so a dual switch with separate channels (TPS22966 VIN1/VOUT1, VIN2/VOUT2) can mark VOUT2 sourced from VIN1 and hide an RS-001. Still present at `8c42799`.

## 2026-11-03 — KH-870: the PDF hashers open with a blocking `open`, so a FIFO at `datasheets/X.pdf` hangs the staleness check

**Severity:** LOW
**File:** `skills/datasheets/datasheet_types/cache_reader.py` (`_compute_pdf_sha256`, `_resolve_pdf_path`); `skills/datasheets/scripts/datasheet_extract_cache.py` (`_pdf_hash`)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-03, product 3.0.x Wave 8c; verified harness-side at `0efc012`. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `b0d9ab6` (3.0.x Wave 9a, unreleased; local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** both hashers opened the cached PDF path with a blocking, link-following `open`, and the resolver returned the path without an `is_file` check.
- **Fix:** a cached PDF path is read only inside the project's `datasheets/` folder and only as a regular file, bounded (`cache_reader.read_regular_bytes`); anything else reads as missing. The silent-stale side effect for paths outside `datasheets/` is filed as KH-905.
- **Verification:** harness probe, FIFO at `datasheets/X.pdf`, 5 s timeout: `_compute_pdf_sha256` and `_pdf_hash` return None at `6009004`, rc 124 (hang) at `9885287`. Waves 9a + 9e gate 2026-11-03 (baseline `9885287`, candidate `6009004`): standard + full-chain strict-field clean, spice-offline identical, distributor-offline 0 differing, tiers 3,575 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-03 — TH-104: `generate_validation_md.py` counted only `### <prefix>-` headings, so closed issues under `## <date> — TH-NNN` headings were dropped and the filed total shrank

**Severity:** LOW (published issue counts in VALIDATION.md)
**File:** `tools/generate_validation_md.py` (`_count_issues`)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-03, the main repo's v3.0.0 release prep: the round-9b draft read "TH-001 through TH-071: 57 filed, 38 closed, 19 open" against 59 / 38 / 21 in the previous VALIDATION.md. **Fixed:** this harness commit (filed and fixed together).

- **Root cause:** only lines starting `### KH-` / `### TH-` were counted, one per heading. FIXED.md entries have been headed `## <date> — <id>:` for some time, so the closed count stopped moving while issues left ISSUES.md. A multi-id heading (`### KH-398 (MEDIUM) / KH-399 (LOW)`) counted once, and a heading that only mentions an id later in its title could set the maximum.
- **Fix:** `_heading_ids` reads the ids a heading opens with, in both formats, including chained ids; counts are distinct ids, and an id still in ISSUES.md stays open even when FIXED.md records a fixed half. Ids later in a title (rule ids such as `TH-001/PDN`, the `Earlier fixes` range heading) are ignored.
- **Verification:** new `tests/test_generate_validation_md.py::test_issue_counts_read_both_heading_formats` failed before the fix and passes after (file 10 / 10). On the round-9b tracker files (`4e665a6f8f0`) the generator now gives KH 450 filed / 378 closed / 72 open (max 496) and TH 73 / 53 / 20 (max 78), matching status.md's "Open 72 KH + 20 TH"; these are the corrected lines given to the main repo for the v3.0.0 VALIDATION.md, applied by hand (draft not regenerated).

## 2026-11-03 — TH-103: `test_kh366_367_determinism` compared the wall-clock `elapsed_s`, so a loaded run could fail a hash-seed determinism check

**Severity:** LOW (spurious pre-push failure)

**Discovered:** 2026-11-03, the pre-push hook of the Waves 8c + 8b adoption push (vs product_0efc012): `test_xv_002_ref_order_stable` failed on `"elapsed_s": 0.001` vs `0.002` between two cross_analysis runs; 12 / 12 standalone reruns passed on 0efc012 and 647bc85. **Fixed:** this harness commit (filed and fixed together).

## 2026-11-03 — KH-806: `analyze_pcb --output` and `diff_analysis --output` are plain writes, and `atomic_write_text` follows a symlinked target

**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analyze_pcb.py` (`--output`), `diff_analysis.py` (`--output`); `kicad_core/fileio.py` (`atomic_write_text`, `resolve()`)

## 2026-11-03 — KH-800: reversing the root-sheet order changes the schematic analyzer's output on 6 of 14 multi-sheet boards

**Severity:** MEDIUM (determinism: the same design gives different nets, findings and a BOM quantity depending on sheet order — wideboy `100p` 6 → 1)
**File:** schematic connectivity / net naming (sheet path), VM-001 domain, multi-driver / ERC, BOM grouping (the handoff names no line)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-31, product 3.0.x Wave 5 handoff follow-up 11 (found while making the diff identity sheet-order-stable, KH-572); repro product `.superpowers/sdd/2026-10-29-v3.0.x-wave5/followups/sheet-order/` (14 boards, `orig.json` / `rev.json` / `diff.json` each); not verified harness-side. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `ff591b3` `dd4e0a8` `a177bcc` `b3f9f0b` `0efc012` (3.0.x Wave 8b, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** equal-rank net names tie-broke on sheet index and child sheets were read in file order, so the stored sheet order changed net names and order-dependent selections.
- **Fix:** equal-rank names tie-break as KiCad 10 (`connection_graph.cpp:3275-3311`): shallower sheet, then the lower full sheet-qualified name, sheet names escaped (`B/C` -> `B{slash}C`); child sheets are read in sheet-uuid order. ## 2026-11-03 — KH-864: EMC limit lookup uses `f_min <= f < f_max`, so a frequency exactly on a band edge (88, 216, 960 MHz FCC; 230 MHz CISPR) takes the upper band's looser limit

**Severity:** LOW (emission margin at four exact frequencies; a harmonic landing on an edge reports 3.5-8 dB more margin than the stricter limit)
**File:** `skills/emc/scripts/emc_formulas.py:88` (`get_emission_limit`), tables `:30-` (`FCC_CLASS_B_RADIATED`, `FCC_CLASS_A_RADIATED`, CISPR tables)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-02, product 3.0.x Wave 8a (slug KH-new-fcc-band-edges); verified harness-side at `647bc85`. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `3fd71c3` `0efc012` (3.0.x Wave 8b, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** `get_emission_limit` took the first band with `f_min <= f < f_max`, so an exact band edge took the upper band's looser limit (and the CISPR 1000 MHz top edge returned None).
- **Fix:** every band containing f, ends included, then the lowest limit (47 CFR 15.209(b) convention); covers FCC 88/216/960, CISPR 230 and 1000 MHz, and CISPR 25 at 68/108 MHz where the upper band is tighter. The SW-001 double count is the KH-643 addendum; the dead SW-003 note is KH-892.
- **Verification:** Wave 8c + 8b gate 2026-11-03 (harness, baseline `647bc85`, candidate `0efc012`, output-changing, budgets `regression/budgets/v30x-wave8b{,-full-chain}.json`): standard + full-chain budgeted clean, 0 residuals, 0 candidate failures; tiers 3,574 / 0 / 8 / 4 vs product_0efc012. 0 corpus movement (standard + full-chain), as the product measured.

## 2026-11-01 — TH-102: the fixture set had no multi-unit schematic, so a placed symbol with unit > 1 could not be pinned by product tests

**Severity:** LOW (coverage gap)
**File:** `tests/fixtures/` (harness fixture set the product's `check_refactor` and `tools/tests` read at the CI pin)
**Discovered:** 2026-11-01, product 3.0.x Wave 7 Task 5 (`test_model_records` could not pin the multi-unit case; ruling R2 substituted a shared-refdes multi-sheet fixture); asked in the Wave 7 close handoff. Filed and fixed by the harness the same day.

- **Root cause:** no fixture placed a symbol with `(unit N>1)`, defined a lib symbol with several units, or carried a legacy `U N>1` line.
- **Fix:** `tests/fixtures/multi-unit/dual_opamp.kicad_sch` (KiCad 9 format, self-authored, no corpus content): U1 (LM358, SOIC-8) placed as unit 1 (follower `SIG_IN` → `BUF_OUT`), unit 2 (non-inverting stage with R1 / R2 on `FB`, output `AMP_OUT`) and unit 3 (`+5V` / `GND` supply pins); nets join through global labels on the pin ends. `tests/test_multi_unit_fixture.py` pins the five component records (U1 ×3, R1, R2), `total_components` 3, and every pin's net. `check_refactor`'s `discover_fixtures` picks the file up, so the product's fixture snapshot gains its artefacts at the next pin bump (re-snapshot the baseline then).
- **Verification:** `tests/test_multi_unit_fixture.py` 2 passed against product_988d576, product_c0a8a62 and product_07b7fb1; tiers vs product_988d576 3,557 / 0 / 8 / 4.

## 2026-11-01 — KH-636: documented commands and workflows fail or destroy user data — `--recursive` sync flag rejected, opencode config corrupted, manual BOM rows deleted, nonexistent Action outputs, repo-relative Deep Review paths, wrong flag precedence

**Severity:** HIGH (user-facing install and skill commands; two of them destroyed user data: the opencode config and manual BOM rows)

**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/05-v3-docs/findings/VERIFICATION.md` do/R3-F3, do/R1-F1, do/R3-F2, do/R1-F4, do/R2-F9, do/R2-F8, do/R3-F5, do/R1-F10). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `821d85c` `1cae2e9` (3.0.x Wave 6, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff); R3-F2 earlier in `3e5a037` (3.0.x Wave 5).

- **Root cause:** the commands and outputs were documented from intent, not from the CLIs' `--help`, `action.yml` or the code paths.
- **Fix:** the bom sync step drops `--recursive` (the sync CLIs follow sub-sheets from the root schematic) and says a second distributor still tries another's misses (true since KH-615); the opencode step creates the global config only when absent and tells the user to edit an existing one by hand; the Action outputs table lists the five real outputs, and `has-critical` is described as set only by EMC / thermal `error` rows (`1cae2e9`, ruling W6-2); the Deep Review gate commands and `datasheet-verification.md` use `<skill-path>` / the digikey sync script; the per-CLI `--output` / `--analysis-dir` rule is stated (ruling W6-1); the annotations step says `design_context.json` is read by Deep Review and nothing is merged (ruling W6-3); the DigiKey section describes the client-credentials flow (no browser, no refresh token). Wave 5 already fixed the R3-F2 re-export line (`3e5a037`; the code twin KH-617).
- **Code questions left open:** Action gating scope → KH-814; output-flag harmonisation → KH-815.
- **Commit-message note:** `821d85c` also carries the KH-329 doc halves (named) and the jlcpcb `<bom-skill-path>` line; `b746033` (final fix wave) states the `plan_extraction` exits.

## 2026-11-01 — KH-637: agent-read kicad references give wrong electrical and geometry formulas — Zener power, IPC-2221 widths, 90°/270° pin rotation, anti-alias criterion, `what_if --target` gain units, boost battery current, and broken manual-fallback parsers

**Severity:** HIGH (agents apply these references during every design review)
**File:** `skills/kicad/references/schematic-analysis.md` (Zener, anti-alias, battery current); `pcb-layout-analysis.md` + `standards-compliance.md` (IPC-2221 tables, TW-001 note); `net-tracing.md` (rotation, mirror); `what-if.md` (`--target`); `manual-pcb-parsing.md` (zone and outline helpers); `manual-gerber-parsing.md` + `gerber-parsing.md` (Excellon decoding)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/05-v3-docs/findings/VERIFICATION.md` do/R2-F1, do/R2-F2, do/R2-F3, do/R2-F4, do/R2-F5, do/R2-F11, do/R2-F6, do/R2-F7). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `46b3d2d` `651a059` `30366d3` `b977a2e` `93f43ea` `46d422b` `1921308`, final fix wave `b7f77be` (3.0.x Wave 6, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff); R2-F5 earlier in `bacf5bc` / `a7ec28f` (3.0.x Wave 5).

- **Root cause:** formulas and snippets written from memory, never recomputed or run against the shared parser.
- **Fix:** Zener dissipation `VZ·IZ` with the series-resistor term stated separately, the anti-alias criterion as f_max well below fs/2, boost battery current `V_load·I_load/(V_bat·η)` (`46b3d2d`); pin positions at 90° / 270° and under mirroring, the one-line mirror rule verified 12/12 with kicad-cli (`651a059`, ruling W6-7); manual zone and outline snippets that return data, including KiCad 5 `filled_polygon` without `(layer)` (`30366d3`, `46d422b`); both IPC-2221 tables recomputed on one basis (1 oz = 35 µm = 1.378 mil, stated by the table) and a TW-001 note that its own table matches neither standard (`b977a2e`, `93f43ea`, ruling W6-5); both drill guides decode Excellon by the declared format, including LZ padding and the Y sign (`1921308`, `b7f77be`). Wave 5 already fixed R2-F5 (linear `--target`, `bacf5bc` / `a7ec28f`).
- **Code questions left open:** TW-001 table provenance → KH-816; the analyzer's LZ drill decoding stays in KH-592 (doc sentence at `gerber-parsing.md:377`, ruling W6-4).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` OK (3 skipped) at `c0a8a62`; `check_refactor quick` vs `baseline-698116c` OK with the empty budget (`budget-empty.json`) and the six `neg__<cli>__schema-noinput` text-allow entries (at `8bb6e0d`); `--schema` x6 description-only (six md5s in handoff-wave6.md); survey oracles rerun at `8bb6e0d`, 66 / 66, 0 mismatches (close-evidence-c0a8a62.md). Harness: re-read in the `c0a8a62` clone (`schematic-analysis.md:339,1020`, `pcb-layout-analysis.md:164`); Wave 6 gate `698116c`..`c0a8a62` — see status.md.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-522: differential-pair `has_esd` set by any shared IC — the USB PHY itself credited as ESD protection (bookkeeping close; GitHub #61.1)

**Severity:** HIGH (default path; a false protection claim on most pairs)
**File:** `schematic/net_analysis.py` (`_detect_differential_pairs`; protection credit at :1409-1411 at `698116c`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R3-F3). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `34767d7` `b6a3d8d` `8ac280b` `5ddf36b` (3.0.x Wave 4 Part A, range `0683d01..d5c500e`); the tracker entry stayed open until the Wave 5 handoff mapped GitHub #61.1 to it.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-571: `what_if` never reaches the patched detection for SPICE, EMC or tolerance, and its crystal fix suggests one cap when the formula is joint

**Severity:** HIGH (what_if CLI; the SPICE and EMC comparisons were empty or "UNKNOWN" on every run)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/what_if.py` (SPICE re-sim input, EMC compare, tolerance fields, `parsed_value`, crystal suggestions, log sweep); `simulate_subcircuits.py:109,135-150`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R12-F2, R12-F3, R12-F8, R12-F5, R12-F9, R12-reg-logsweep). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `aba7a08` `bacf5bc` `a7ec28f`, CHANGELOG correction `86230cc` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** the SPICE re-sim passed `signal_analysis`, which `simulate_subcircuits` reads only in its pre-v1.3 guard, so both runs saw the original values; the EMC compare read `overall_risk` / `risk_level`, which no output carries; tolerance fields came from the nominal deltas only; `parsed_value` was treated as a dict though the producer emits a scalar; the two crystal-cap suggestions were one joint edit; a zero log-sweep bound raised ZeroDivisionError.
- **Fix:** `--spice` simulates the changed subcircuit with the patched values; `--emc` previews EMC on the patched design (`before_risk` / `after_risk` = `summary.emc_risk_score`, a new `worsened` list, findings matched as `diff_analysis` matches them); new `--offline` flag; `--spice` with a sweep exits 2. Tolerance corners cover every recalculable field; `--suggest-fixes` sizes both crystal caps together; a log-sweep bound ≤ 0 exits 2; patched detections recompute time constant, crystal load error / status and regulator `power_dissipation`; `--output` replaces each patched finding in place and writes UTF-8 atomically (one atomic text writer in `kicad_core`, `a7ec28f`). `what_if --spice` without `--offline` can now query distributors (CHANGELOG `### Changed`, `86230cc`).
- **Commit-message note:** `bacf5bc` / `a7ec28f` also carry the KH-585 what_if half (UTF-8 I/O) and the KH-637 `what-if.md` `--target` doc fix without naming them.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). Harness: 3.0.x Wave 5 gate `40b8ff3`..`698116c` (2026-10-31; candidate pushed, origin/v3.0.x-dev = `698116c`): FULL standard budgeted clean (149,633 compared, 5,078 moved, 175,794 deltas, 0 residuals, 0 candidate failures); full-chain GATE PASS (21,409 compared, 1,434 moved, 0 residuals); spice-offline identical 8,830/8,830; text oracle 916 / 54 allowed; `--schema` x6 identical; distributor-offline 62 runs, differences exactly the 42 declared re-frozen + new runs; tiers vs product_698116c 3,562 / 0 / 8 / 4 — see status.md.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-572: diff drops rich findings without a `reference`/`detection_id` and counts only entities, so VD-001 additions and routing-only regressions report "No changes detected"

**Severity:** HIGH (every PR through the Action; also drives the analysis cache's new-run decision)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/diff_engine.py` (`_get_key` / `_generic_identity`, `_diff_lists`, totals, severity, footprint `lib_id`, EMC severity); `diff_analysis.py` (`has_changes`); `action/format-report.py`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R12-F1, R12-F4, R12-reg-libid). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `c4516f0` `031272d` `ca4d97f` `463c523` `44b80f0`, CHANGELOG correction `86230cc` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** `_diff_lists` dropped items whose key was None (VD-001 carries only `components` / `nets` / `finding_id`); `has_changes` followed an entity-only count, so routing- or statistics-only changes read "No changes detected"; footprints were compared on a `lib_id` corpus PCBs do not carry; EMC severity read flat legacy keys.
- **Fix:** every finding (schematic, PCB, EMC, thermal) is compared by identity — `finding_id` unless positional (`#N` suffix, `__unnamed_N` net), then content — and footprint swaps are reported; PCB diffs gain a `findings` section; EMC counts come from `summary.by_severity`. `has_changes` is true when any section changed; `total_changes` counts listed items and the moved scalars go to a new `summary.metric_changes`; a higher EMC risk score is an improvement (0 = worst); routing changes are major (new `--analysis-dir` run). The Action PR comment carries the PCB diff and the added/removed rows and escapes `|` and mentions.
- **Commit-message note:** `ca4d97f` also carries the KH-585 diff half (`--output` UTF-8) without naming it.
- **Harness note:** handoff ask 5 — `tests/test_diff_analysis.py::test_regression_emc_risk_score_increase` and `::test_no_regressions_on_improvements` flip.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). Harness: 3.0.x Wave 5 gate `40b8ff3`..`698116c` (2026-10-31; candidate pushed, origin/v3.0.x-dev = `698116c`): FULL standard budgeted clean (149,633 compared, 5,078 moved, 175,794 deltas, 0 residuals, 0 candidate failures); full-chain GATE PASS (21,409 compared, 1,434 moved, 0 residuals); spice-offline identical 8,830/8,830; text oracle 916 / 54 allowed; `--schema` x6 identical; distributor-offline 62 runs, differences exactly the 42 declared re-frozen + new runs; tiers vs product_698116c 3,562 / 0 / 8 / 4 — see status.md.

**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/lifecycle_audit.py` (`project_dir` from `analysis["file"]`, `read_extraction_temperature`); `kicad_core/project.py` (shared resolver)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R14-X1). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `9b1e23e` `1a8d01e` `96c5935` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** the schematic envelope no longer carries `file`, so `project_dir` became the JSON's own directory and the extraction lookup read `analysis/<run_id>/datasheets/extracted/`, which never exists; a `null` or non-dict extraction raised. Same root cause as KH-477 (fixed for SPICE only).
- **Fix:** the project directory comes from the analysis `inputs.source_files` (`kicad_core.project.project_dir_from_analysis`, also used by KH-782); current (v2) extractions supply the ambient operating range, never junction, storage or case ranges; a malformed extraction is skipped with a warning and `analyze_schematic.py --lifecycle` no longer crashes on one; reversed bounds read in order, a Fahrenheit range is not read as Celsius, fractional lead weeks round up. The thermal `file` fallback named in the entry moved with KH-782 (`7416758`).
- **Commit-message note:** `9b1e23e`..`96c5935` also carry the KH-585 lifecycle UTF-8 lines without naming them.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-580: the Deep Review evidence gate certifies numerically different quotes (`55 V` vs `5.5 V`, `-40 C` vs `40 C`, `<` vs `>`, `"..."`) and crashes on non-dict evidence

**Severity:** HIGH (Deep Review gate default path; a wrong quote was stamped `evidence_checked: full`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/review/scripts/deep_review_gate.py` (`_quote_in_text`, `check_datasheet`, `gate_finding`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R14-F1, R14-F4, nonpositive-page register item). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `dbee622` `d11de33` `79e0273` `316bd87` `bc31fc0` `c2a6fa8` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** the squash normalisation dropped digits' context, signs, decimal points and comparison operators, and an all-punctuation quote returned True; non-dict evidence or `findings` raised instead of quarantining; a page ≤ 0 checked the whole document.
- **Fix:** a quote that differs from the page in a number, sign, decimal point, comparison operator or unit letter (`µ`, `Ω`) is quarantined ("55 V" vs "5.5 V", "40 °C" vs "−40 °C", "15 V" vs "±15 V", "10 µA" vs "10 A"); case, spacing, punctuation, Unicode minus/dash spellings and hyphenation stay tolerated. A quote with no letter or digit, a page below 1 or past the end, and non-object evidence are quarantined; a non-array `findings` / `quarantined` or an unreadable analysis JSON is an input error (exit 2). UTF-8 I/O; atomic writes with the umask mode that replace a symlink.
- **Remainder → KH-807:** a spaced "± 15 V" on the page still certifies a "15 V" quote.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). ## 2026-10-31 — KH-595: `export_issues` dedups by rule label only, so the first export opens N issues per rule and later runs skip every new instance of an already-open rule

**Severity:** MEDIUM (visible `SKIP` lines; GitHub issue creation)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/export_issues.py` (skip logic, rule-label dedup key, failed lookup returns `[]`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R12-F7). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `26f8177` `cca2a4c` `6cb75e0` `f502701` `79be0b6` `c265a2a` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** issues were keyed by the rule label, with no dedup inside a run, and a failed open-issue lookup returned `[]`, so everything was re-filed.
- **Fix:** issues are matched by finding (ruling W5-13): each body starts with a hidden `finding_id` marker carrying a content key, so renumbered unnamed nets and reordered collision suffixes do not duplicate; claims run in two passes so a finding never takes another present finding's issue; issues without a marker are matched once by exact title; `@mentions` are neutralised; a failed or full-page `gh issue list` exits 1 and exports nothing.
- **Remainder → KH-812:** 1000+ open issues refuse the export (no paging).

## 2026-10-31 — KH-596: a re-run with `--analysis-dir` mixes a fresh schematic.json with stale pcb/thermal outputs in the new run, and `source_hashes` drops the PCB hash

**Severity:** MEDIUM (documented `--analysis-dir` workflow; cache coherence)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analysis_cache.py` (copy-forward, `_OUTPUT_SOURCE_EXT`, stale-skipped `outputs` entries, hashes)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (kc/R13-F1). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `4c8e838` `53a917c` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** derived outputs (thermal / EMC / cross-analysis / SPICE) were copied forward without checking the inputs they were built from, and `source_hashes` kept only the re-run analyzer's source.
- **Fix:** when a schematic or PCB re-run changes `schematic.json` / `pcb.json`, every derived output built from the old file (from its `inputs.upstream_artifacts`; SPICE counts as built from both) leaves the run, with a stderr `Note:`; a reproducing re-run keeps them; `source_hashes` keep every source behind the run's outputs; an output not carried forward leaves `outputs` (ruling W5-14).
- **Remainder → KH-805:** `lifecycle.json` is still carried forward after a BOM change, and `gerber.json` is never judged stale.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). ## 2026-10-31 — KH-603: BOM manager reads `POPULATE=1` as DNP, and a group's DNP state comes from its first member, so the order file depends on symbol file order

**Severity:** HIGH (default `bom_manager` export/order path; POPULATE projects lost every fitted part)
**File:** `skills/bom/scripts/bom_manager.py` (`is_dnp`, `DNP_FIELDS`, group keys)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R5-F4, sk/R5-F1). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `92d265c` `da6fa70`, close fix wave `698116c` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** every `DNP_FIELDS` entry, `POPULATE` included, was tested against `("YES","TRUE","1","DNP")` before the POPULATE-specific `"0"` check, so `POPULATE=1` read as DNP.
- **Fix:** `POPULATE` is a population flag: `1`, `yes`, `true` or empty = fitted; `0`, `no`, `false`, `n`, `DNP`, `DNF`, `do not fit`, `do not populate`, `not fitted`, `unfitted` (whole value, any case) = not fitted, so a part number containing `DNP` stays fitted. `698116c` makes this one list shared with the JLCPCB translator (KH-604).
- **Group half:** already fixed before this range — at `7131f26` the group key carries the DNP state ("A line never mixes DNP and fitted parts", CHANGELOG kf/A13-F4).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). Harness: 3.0.x Wave 5 gate `40b8ff3`..`698116c` (2026-10-31; candidate pushed, origin/v3.0.x-dev = `698116c`): FULL standard budgeted clean (149,633 compared, 5,078 moved, 175,794 deltas, 0 residuals, 0 candidate failures); full-chain GATE PASS (21,409 compared, 1,434 moved, 0 residuals); spice-offline identical 8,830/8,830; text oracle 916 / 54 allowed; `--schema` x6 identical; distributor-offline 62 runs, differences exactly the 42 declared re-frozen + new runs; tiers vs product_698116c 3,562 / 0 / 8 / 4 — see status.md.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-614: re-planning a datasheet extraction after a PDF revision reuses the old task results and stamps them with the new PDF's SHA

**Severity:** HIGH (opt-in extraction pipeline; defeated the only staleness guard)
**File:** `skills/datasheets/scripts/plan_extraction.py`, `merge_results.py` (`_read_result`, `_classify`, `_initial_extraction`); `references/dispatcher-contract.md`, `dispatch-claude-code.md`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R3-F2). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `306d227` `28443cc` `9ae577b` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** results were not bound to a PDF; the merger checked status and schema only and stamped the new plan's SHA and a fresh timestamp on old results.
- **Fix:** task results carry `pdf_sha256` (copied from the plan); `merge_results.py` rejects a result without it or from another PDF revision; re-planning for a changed PDF removes the previous results; `--use-cached-scout` refuses a scout from a different PDF and warns about one with no SHA (ruling W5-10). Results written before this change need one re-dispatch.
- **Harness note:** handoff ask 2 — `tests/contract/test_merge_results.py` ×5 need `pdf_sha256` in the wrappers and in `tests/fixtures/datasheets/result-regulator-complete.example.json`.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-615: distributor sync marks a PDF transport failure as permanent, one provider's failure blocks every other provider, and LCSC sync never tries the direct lookup

**Severity:** MEDIUM (default distributor sync; missing datasheets, recoverable with `--force`)
**File:** `skills/datasheets/distributor_core/download.py`, `sync.py` (outcome recording, skip logic, `--force-all`); `provider_digikey.py`; `skills/lcsc/scripts/provider_lcsc.py` (`sync_one_part`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R4-F2, sk/R4-F3, sk/R4-F7). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `5061fe5` `bc6ce0d` `ea5f639` `9e60522` `9b2106d` `a14af98` `590e5f3` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** a download failure without an exception returned False → permanent `failed`; `--force-all` overwrote a prior `ok`; failures carried no provider, so one provider's miss skipped the part at every other provider; LCSC sync had no direct lookup.
- **Fix:** one outcome helper for serial and parallel sync (`5061fe5`); network failures are recorded `error` with the distributor's message and retried next run (refusals, size / time limits, unwritable files and redirect loops stay permanent); `--force-all` keeps the existing entry and file when the refresh fails; failures are recorded per provider (`failed_providers`, ruling W5-4) and legacy unattributed failures are retried once by each distributor; LCSC sync looks up an unlisted code on LCSC's product page and keeps it only when LCSC answers with that code; element14 goes on to its SKU and keyword searches after a wrong-part hit; DigiKey 429 stops after three retries (KH-492 rider, `ea5f639`). Distributor-offline: `590e5f3` re-freeze; new `sync-second-provider` ×4 (`a14af98`), `sync-force-all` ×4 (`ea5f639`, `9e60522`), `lcsc/sync-lcsc-direct` (`ea5f639`).
- **Remainder → KH-813:** `--force-all` dropping an entry for a real answer leaves the old PDF on disk.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). ## 2026-10-31 — KH-616: distributor sync loses worker exceptions under `--parallel`, schedules a repeated MPN twice with colliding `.part` files, and `--json` output is preceded by a stdout progress line

**Severity:** MEDIUM (opt-in `--parallel` / `--json`; multi-row MPNs on the default path)
**File:** `skills/datasheets/distributor_core/sync.py`, `inputs.py` (`extract_parts`), `download.py`; `provider_element14.py`; the fetch CLIs
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R4-F4, sk/R4-F6, sk/R4-F5). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `430abd7` `0dff5f0` `c650abf` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

## 2026-10-31 — KH-620: `datasheet_verify` decoupling counts the X5R/X7R digit (and `max`) as a capacitor quantity, pools caps across every power pin with no input/output split, and orders `actual_caps` by set iteration

**Severity:** MEDIUM (legacy v1.3-shaped caches only)
**File:** `skills/datasheets/scripts/datasheet_verify.py` (quantity regex, `power_pin_nets`, cap pooling)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R3-F5, sk/R3-F6). **Fixed:** order half 3.0.x Wave 2 `c40e135`; rest product v3.0.x-dev `ac99c1b` `c8a2f62` `4e9c48d` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** the quantity regex took any digit run (`X5R` → 5, `max 10mm` → 10); caps were pooled across every power-pin net with no role split or ground check.
- **Fix:** the X5R/X7R digit, "max" and pad sizes are not counts; "2 x 10uF", "22uFx2" and "10μF" are read. Input and output recommendations are checked on the pins of their role (a `passive` or direction-less power pin takes its role from its function or name); a cap counts only when its other end is on ground (a ground-named net or one of the IC's own ground pins).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). ## 2026-10-31 — KH-621: `datasheet_verify` v2 pin adapter keeps only the first of grouped pin numbers, uses the domain limit before the per-pin `recommended`, and ignores `is_5v_tolerant`

**Severity:** MEDIUM (current v2 pipeline, default verifier path)
**File:** `skills/datasheets/scripts/datasheet_verify.py` (v2 pin adapter, `pin_voltage_abs_max_exceeded`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R3-F7, sk/R3-F12). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `050e963` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

## 2026-10-31 — KH-484: GR-002 compares layer extent SIZES, not offsets — a layer shifted by any amount with the same bounding-box size passes the alignment check

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analyze_gerbers.py` (`check_alignment`, extents walker); `methodology_gerbers.md`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-24, v3 round-9b handoff §7 item 5 (review A-I12); addenda 2026-10-25 (kc/R10-reg-GR002units; Wave 2 inner-plane panels) and 2026-10-29 (five FND locks). **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `0c6a506` `4deebc0`, close fix wave `9da1f46` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** `check_alignment` compared the spread of per-layer widths / heights against 5 % / 2 mm in each layer's own units and never compared origins, so a shifted layer passed, an inch layer got a 2-inch tolerance, and panels whose inner planes sit inside the panel extent warned.
- **Fix:** GR-002 reports copper outside the board outline: a copper layer past the Edge.Cuts extent by more than max(2 mm, 5 % of that side) is named with its distance. Extents are millimetres for every file (`alignment.layer_extents` now mm for inch files, as the schema states); arcs and full circles count their full sweep; several outline files together bound the board; a one-axis Edge.Cuts file is not the outline (`9da1f46`); drill files are not compared (ruling W5-21, kc/R10-F5). Budget (standard): GR-002 −98 on 58 modern units and −85 legacy, `aligned` F → T 107/300, T → F 0, `board_dimensions` 11/300.
- **Addendum (2026-10-29 FND locks):** the five locks named in the ISSUES addendum (`FND-00001817-AST-01`, `FND-00001451-AST-03`, `FND-00001455-AST-03`, `FND-00001488-AST-03`, `FND-00001576-AST-01`; handoff: "the 5-6 FND units") are expected to flip back to `aligned` True.
- **Corpus confirmation (2026-11-03, v3.0.1 regen at `9885287`):** the five 2026-10-29 FND locks now PASS; six other FND locks that had pinned `aligned == False` on findings calling that value wrong (FND-00001727-AST-02, 00002233-AST-01, 00001344-AST-05, 00001717-AST-01, 00001440-AST-03, 00001743-AST-02) were re-anchored to True on the product's ruling; SEED `alignment.aligned` locks moved on 2,053 gerber units (= the Wave 5 class). Pattern filed as TH-105.
- **Remainder → KH-802:** outline choice (a larger stale outline can swallow real outside copper), `compute_board_dimensions` takes the first Edge.Cuts file, G70 files without `%MO`, `%FST` / incremental extents.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). Harness: 3.0.x Wave 5 gate `40b8ff3`..`698116c` (2026-10-31; candidate pushed, origin/v3.0.x-dev = `698116c`): FULL standard budgeted clean (149,633 compared, 5,078 moved, 175,794 deltas, 0 residuals, 0 candidate failures); full-chain GATE PASS (21,409 compared, 1,434 moved, 0 residuals); spice-offline identical 8,830/8,830; text oracle 916 / 54 allowed; `--schema` x6 identical; distributor-offline 62 runs, differences exactly the 42 declared re-frozen + new runs; tiers vs product_698116c 3,562 / 0 / 8 / 4 — see status.md.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-782: analyzers read datasheet extractions from a shared temporary directory, or from `datasheets/extracted` beside the input JSON or the project's parent folder

**Severity:** MEDIUM (Security: a planted extraction in a shared or parent directory reached analysis output)
**File:** `skills/datasheets/scripts/datasheet_extract_cache.py` (`resolve_extract_dir`, fallback `$TMPDIR/kicad-happy/datasheets/extracted`), `datasheet_features.py`; `analyze_thermal.py`; `lifecycle_audit.py`; `skills/emc/scripts/emc_rules.py`; `skills/spice/scripts/spice_model_cache.py`; `datasheet_verify.py` (`_resolve_extract_dir`, parent-folder attempt, manifest read); `kicad_core/project.py`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-29, product 3.0.x Wave 5 datasheets survey § 9, widened by the lifecycle survey (slug KH-new-tmp-extract-cache); the verifier half found by the whole-range close review (Important I1). Assigned FIXED-direct, never open. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `b212241` `7416758` `84cc723` `02550ea`, close fix wave `b5649f7` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** with no project named, `resolve_extract_dir` fell back to one shared `$TMPDIR` cache; thermal and lifecycle looked beside the input JSON (a JSON in `/tmp` read `/tmp/datasheets/extracted`); the schematic verifier also tried the project's parent folder and read the manifest without the symlink refusal and size cap.
- **Fix:** the project comes from the analysis `inputs.source_files` (a relative path only when that schematic exists from the cwd); with none there is no extraction cache. Thermal finds the project's cache from an `analysis/<run>/schematic.json`; the SPICE datasheet-spec fallback reads only the named project; the verifier reads only the project's own `datasheets/extracted` and its `manifest.json` with the symlink refusal and size cap (`b5649f7`). CHANGELOG `### Security`.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 2,108 OK (3 skipped) at `698116c`; `check_refactor quick` vs `7131f26` OK on all 8 checks with the union budget (`budget-wave5-union.json`, 43 classes) and the union text-allow list; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `7131f26` (handoff-wave5.md, close-evidence-698116c.md). Harness: 3.0.x Wave 5 gate `40b8ff3`..`698116c` (2026-10-31; candidate pushed, origin/v3.0.x-dev = `698116c`): FULL standard budgeted clean (149,633 compared, 5,078 moved, 175,794 deltas, 0 residuals, 0 candidate failures); full-chain GATE PASS (21,409 compared, 1,434 moved, 0 residuals); spice-offline identical 8,830/8,830; text oracle 916 / 54 allowed; `--schema` x6 identical; distributor-offline 62 runs, differences exactly the 42 declared re-frozen + new runs; tiers vs product_698116c 3,562 / 0 / 8 / 4 — see status.md.

## 2026-10-31 — KH-784: Gerber completeness ignores inner copper a job file implies and misreads KiCad 9.0.0-9.0.4 job inner-layer numbering

**Severity:** MEDIUM (missing inner layers unreported; complete KiCad 9.0.0-9.0.4 sets reported missing `In4.Cu` / `In6.Cu`)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/analyze_gerbers.py` (`check_completeness`, `_build_gerber_findings`, `identify_layer_type`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 (kf/A12-F1), carried as a new KH by the product 3.0.x Wave 5 plan with the KiCad 9.0.0-9.0.4 job-id bug (fixed upstream in KiCad `9725ac2215`, first tag 9.0.5) (slug KH-new-gerber-completeness); assigned FIXED-direct, never open. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `e67a1c2` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

## 2026-10-31 — KH-785: the Gerber X2 reader misses `%TO.P` pad components, `G04 #@!` structured-comment attributes, `\uXXXX` escapes and non-round aperture shapes

## 2026-10-31 — KH-786: Gerber-format drill files, `.xln` / `.nc` files and Excellon route slots are not counted as drills, and a directory named `*.drl` crashes the analyzer

**Severity:** MEDIUM (false GR-003 "no drill" warnings on Gerber-drill exports; KeyError crash)

## 2026-10-31 — KH-787: an empty return-path result is dropped from the PCB output, so EMC GP-001 asks for `--full` on boards that ran it (GitHub #60.1)

## 2026-10-31 — KH-789: USB connectors are read as Type-C by a plain substring of value / footprint / lib_id, and CC checks run on connectors without CC pins (GitHub #61.2)

**Severity:** MEDIUM (false Type-C CC findings on non-Type-C connectors)
**File:** `skills/kicad/scripts/schematic/system_analyses.py:2198-2203` at `7131f26` (`USB_C` / `USBC` / `TYPE-C` / `TYPE_C` / `TYPEC` substring test)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-30, GitHub #61 item 2 (PGIRang; the trigger is lib_id `Fixture:USB_CONN`, not the reporter's `USB_B` value) (slug KH-new-typec-detect); assigned FIXED-direct, never open. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `aeca1b0` `e3333d7` `472a9b3`, CHANGELOG correction `86230cc` (3.0.x Wave 5, unreleased; commits local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Root cause:** a substring match (`USB_CON…`, `USBCON…`, `USB_CAN_SW`, `USB_COMBINED`; ~16 units / ~8 repos) made a connector Type-C, and CC pins were never required. Corpus at `40b8ff3`: 4,156 USB connectors, 2,317 `is_type_c`, 59 (28 repos) without a CC pin.
- **Fix:** Type-C by a name token or CC pins (one token rule); CC checks only on connectors with CC pins; an unreadable CC resistor value is info, not a missing pull-down; every spec Rp within tolerance counts (56k/36k ±20 %, 22k/12k/10k ±5 %; 4.7k from 4465 Ω to under 4800 Ω); a 4.8k-5.6k Rd is never Rp; a DNP resistor is absent; a plug's single CC pin is one side. Budget (standard): `usb_compliance.connectors[]` incl. kind `type`, UC-003 +55 / 27 units, −87 / 36 units on a 392-unit A/B, rollups.

## 2026-10-28 — KH-675: `rail_voltages` takes a negative regulator estimate for a positive-named rail; since KH-519 its consumers use the wrong magnitude

**Severity:** MEDIUM
**File:** `signal_detectors.py` regulator detection (inverting decision, Vref source, estimate provenance) → `rail_voltages`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-26, harness, Wave 3 gate adjudication. **Fixed (partly):** product v3.0.x-dev `6ecc059` (3.0.x Wave 4 Part A, unreleased; SHAs local and unpushed at the handoff, they change if the user rewords commits before the push, the tip tree stays `b31d4ff`'s).

- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 1,391 OK (4 skips); `check_refactor quick` OK per task against rolling baselines, whole-range `budget-compare` OK (29 claimed in 7 fixture classes, 0 unclaimed); `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1` (handoff-wave4-A.md). **Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (sk/R2-N4, R2-F1, R2-F2, R2-F4). **Fixed (partly):** product v3.0.x-dev `8773b64` `6e50694` `404f719` (3.0.x Wave 4 Part A, unreleased; SHAs local and unpushed at the handoff).

- **Remainder → KH-716:** inrush now measures `i_peak` but still passes without comparing it with `estimated_inrush_A`.

## 2026-10-27 — KH-426: XV-001..003 never compare MPN schematic ↔ PCB — 17 stale footprint MPNs and `BSS138LT1G` vs `BSS138` on the SacMap board produce 0 findings

**Severity:** MEDIUM

**Discovered:** 2026-10-05, SacMap rev2 run-8 soak; filed by the harness 2026-10-06. **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `b43a818` / `0520727` (3.0.x Wave 3b Part B, unreleased).

- **Correction to the entry:** the fix is a new rule **XV-004** (`check_mpn_parity`, its own `checks_run` entry). **XV-003** compares footprints (schematic footprint field vs board FPID, `check_cross_validation`): documented since v1.3, emitted since `b43a818`. The title's "XV-001..003 compare value/footprint only" was the pre-fix state; XV-001 compares references, XV-002 values, XV-003 footprints, XV-004 MPNs. The compare is exact after `strip()` on both sides (KiCad copies fields exactly, `board_netlist_updater.cpp:523-548`), not case-insensitive as the fix direction suggested (no case-only drift in 569 drifted refs), and fires only when both MPNs are non-blank (ruling 47). A symbol MPN with a blank board MPN on a KiCad 6+ board is not reported.
- **Fix:** parts pair by schematic path, as Update PCB does (R31), with a reference fallback for footprints whose path names no symbol; XV-004 compares MPNs. The SacMap `BSS138` vs `BSS138LT1G` case is a product test. Corpus: classes X2 / X4 (and X3 for XV-003).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 999 OK (4 skips); `check_refactor.py quick` OK 8/8 over the range with the union budget; `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1` (handoff-wave3b-B.md). ## 2026-10-26 — TH-098: the required-tier skip guard fails a run when an external tool (pdftotext, ngspice) is missing

**Severity:** MEDIUM (product CI harness-smoke exited 1 at pin `f54f2cd462a` with every test passing)
**File:** `conftest.py` (`pytest_runtest_makereport` / `pytest_sessionfinish`, the unlisted-skip guard); `tests/known_skips.json`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-26, by the main-repo agent on GitHub's runner (product v3.0.x-dev `022361b`): three tool-gated skips were not in the allowlist. The TH-097 sweep (PATH stripped of ngspice / kicad-cli) missed it because its exit code was not checked — the guard fails the session after the summary line. **Fixed:** harness, same day.

- **Root cause:** `tests/contract/test_deep_review_gate.py::test_datasheet_quote_check`, `tests/test_kh384_385_gate.py::test_kh385_elided_quote_passes_fabricated_quote_quarantines_with_nearest_match` (pdftotext) and `tests/contract/test_kh345_spice_text_flag.py::test_text_output_is_not_json` (ngspice) skip when their tool is absent, and the guard treats every unlisted skip in `unit` / `offline_contract` as a failure.
- **Fix (decision):** list the three in `tests/known_skips.json` with reason "external tool: … not installed", rather than let the guard accept skips by reason text: the guard exists to catch quiet skips, and a reason-pattern exemption would pass any test that wrongly reports a missing tool. A new tool-gated test must be listed the same way. The product also installs ngspice + poppler-utils in that CI job (`622d348`), so on CI the tests run.
- **Verification:** `unit or offline_contract` vs product_d2b9e72 with pdftotext, ngspice, kicad-cli, ltspice and xyce removed from PATH: 3,493 passed / 11 skipped / 4 xfailed, **exit 0** (before: exit 1, "unlisted skips in required tiers (3)").

## 2026-10-26 — TH-097: `run/run_spice.py` checks for ngspice before validating the selection, so `test_unqualified_run_exits_2_without_all` fails on runners without ngspice

**Severity:** MEDIUM (product CI harness-smoke red at pin `bd551df5b41`: product v3.0.x-dev run 40414345709, 1 failed / 3,491 passed)
**File:** `run/run_spice.py` (`main`: the ngspice check at :236 ran before `expand_selection`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-26, by the main-repo agent on GitHub's runner (no ngspice); the ordering dates from the wave 10 runner refactor (`9acba65938f`). Locally green only because ngspice is installed. **Fixed:** harness, same day.

- **Root cause:** a run with no selection is a usage error that `expand_selection` reports with exit 2, but the simulator check ran first and exited 1 when ngspice was missing, so the usage error's exit code depended on the environment.
- **Fix:** `expand_selection` runs first; the ngspice check follows it, still before `retire_orphaned_outputs`, so a missing simulator writes nothing. New `test_usage_error_does_not_depend_on_ngspice` runs the runner with an empty PATH and no `NGSPICE_PATH`.
- **Verification:** the new test is red without the fix and green with it; `unit or offline_contract` vs product_d2b9e72 with `ngspice`, `kicad-cli`, `ltspice` and `xyce` removed from PATH: 3,495 passed / 0 failed / 9 skipped / 4 xfailed (the extra skip is `tests/contract/test_kh345_spice_text_flag.py`, a deliberate "ngspice not installed" skip; no test needs kicad-cli in these tiers).

## 2026-10-26 — KH-510: `_tokenize` gives a quoted `")"` / `"("` the same token as punctuation, so valid files with a lone bracket in a string swallow the following symbols

**Severity:** HIGH (valid input; every parser consumer, schematic and PCB)
**File:** `kicad_core/sexp.py:77` (`_tokenize`, quoted string appended as a bare `str`); compared as punctuation at `:94` / `:97` (`parse`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R1-F1) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `e79b849` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** `parse('(kicad_sch (text ")") (symbol (lib_id "Device:R")))')` → `['kicad_sch', ['text']]`. On `ccadic/TI92-revive/ti92revive/keyboard.kicad_sch` (keycap values `(property "Value" "(")` at :1461 and `")"` at :1583) the file has 86 placed `(symbol (lib_id` blocks but parsing yields 78 top-level `symbol` lists; the ones in between are nested into a bogus list. About 26 corpus `.kicad_sch` / `.kicad_pcb` files hold a lone quoted `"("` / `")"` (a few false hits on escaped quotes). Distinct from KH-482, which is malformed input.
- **Fix:** Punctuation tokens are sentinels (`_LPAREN` / `_RPAREN`), so a quoted `"("` / `")"` stays a plain string; the parser's list-of-str output is unchanged. Corpus (class M1): schematic 2 units / 1 repo, pcb 13 units / 8 repos carry a lone quoted bracket and moved.
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 664 OK (8 skips); `check_refactor.py quick` vs the `79420eb` snapshot 8/8 OK (fixture JSON deltas only in the declared classes, 2 allowed text artefacts); `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1`; kicad-cli / KiCad-5 netlist / DRC oracles (handoff-wave3.md). Harness: Wave 3 gate `004bba5`..`d2b9e72` — see status.md; per-unit labels `results/v30x_w3_gate/field_report_budgeted_v30x-wave3_streamed.units.jsonl`, class summary `results/v30x_w3_gate/class_summary.json`.

## 2026-10-26 — KH-511: legacy `.sch` pin positions invert Y twice under a raw TRANSFORM matrix and skip matrices starting with `-`; `_snap_pins_to_wires` then moves correctly placed pins to the nearest wire end

**Severity:** HIGH (default path, every legacy KiCad 5 schematic)
**File:** `schematic/reader.py:205-228` (`compute_pin_positions`: raw-matrix branch `rpy = c*px + d*py` at :208, then `abs_y = cy - rpy` at :228); `schematic/legacy_reader.py:664` (`_parse_legacy_single_sheet`, `cl[0].isdigit()` drops matrix lines like `\t-1 0 0 1`); `schematic/legacy_reader.py:465-541` (`_snap_pins_to_wires`, sole caller `schematic/pipeline.py:970`, passes every component)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R2-F1, kc/R2-F2) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `562706a, 81a13b7, fd17ee3` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** KiCad legacy applies TRANSFORM as pos + T·p (default `1 0 0 -1` already flips Y); the code flips again. Share of pins landing on a wire endpoint before snapping, current code vs corrected convention: ltc3331.sch 79/110 vs 109/110; dtnking STM32F401CCT6.sch 99/150 vs 141/150 (74 matrix lines, several starting `-1`); clock.sch 32/68 vs 38/68; TemperatureHumidityEPD 60/66 vs 64/66. The snap pass hides much of this: its docstring (:468-471) says it exists for built-in fallback offsets, but it has no `_pin_source` guard and skips only power/flag types (:492), so any pin not on a wire endpoint (on an NC marker, a label, or another pin) is moved to the nearest endpoint within 12 mm in the pin direction (:528-539).
- **Fix:** TRANSFORM applied once as KiCad does, matrix lines starting with `-` read, angle / mirror recomputed from the matrix; `_snap_pins_to_wires` moves only built-in fallback pins onto free wire ends (`_pin_source` gains `builtin`, `pin_source_coverage.builtin_fallback`). Corpus (class L1): all 10,845 legacy schematic units / 2,209 repos moved (label L); pin positions or `_pin_source` moved on 9,303, net grouping on 9,064. Against the KiCad-5 netlists shipped beside 2,233 legacy roots whose ref set matches: clean boards 100 -> 1,855, split rows 76,416 -> 2,516, merged rows 55,585 -> 571; 6 boards score worse (KH-677).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 664 OK (8 skips); `check_refactor.py quick` vs the `79420eb` snapshot 8/8 OK (fixture JSON deltas only in the declared classes, 2 allowed text artefacts); `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1`; kicad-cli / KiCad-5 netlist / DRC oracles (handoff-wave3.md). Harness: Wave 3 gate `004bba5`..`d2b9e72` — see status.md; per-unit labels `results/v30x_w3_gate/field_report_budgeted_v30x-wave3_streamed.units.jsonl`, class summary `results/v30x_w3_gate/class_summary.json`.

## 2026-10-26 — KH-512: the legacy library parser drops the pin visibility and De Morgan `convert` fields — hidden power pins never join their rail and both body styles merge

**Severity:** HIGH (default path, legacy schematics with hidden power pins or De Morgan symbols)
**File:** `schematic/legacy_reader.py:266-289` (`_parse_legacy_lib`: pin dicts carry no `hidden` key, `parts[12]` (shape/visibility, `N` = invisible) is never read, `parts[10]` (convert) is discarded); consumer `schematic/connectivity.py:529-540` (`build_net_map` legacy implicit-power pass, which therefore never fires)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R2-F6, kc/R2-F3 legacy half) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `1c0e975, 15d23b4` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** the corpus `*-cache.lib` files hold 6,756 hidden VCC/GND/VDD/VSS `power_in` pins (`W N`); the implicit-power pass, whose comment names exactly this case, joins none of them to their rail. A De Morgan symbol's two body styles both contribute pins, giving duplicate pin entries per unit (the modern twin is KH-515).
- **Fix:** The legacy library parser reads pin visibility (`hidden: true`) and the `convert` field; one body style per placed symbol; legacy hidden power pins join their rail. Corpus (class L2): 1,424 legacy units gain `hidden` pins or lose body-2 duplicates (inside label L).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 664 OK (8 skips); `check_refactor.py quick` vs the `79420eb` snapshot 8/8 OK (fixture JSON deltas only in the declared classes, 2 allowed text artefacts); `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1`; kicad-cli / KiCad-5 netlist / DRC oracles (handoff-wave3.md). Harness: Wave 3 gate `004bba5`..`d2b9e72` — see status.md; per-unit labels `results/v30x_w3_gate/field_report_budgeted_v30x-wave3_streamed.units.jsonl`, class summary `results/v30x_w3_gate/class_summary.json`.

## 2026-10-26 — KH-513: legacy `$Sheet` blocks drop their F2+ sheet-pin records and child HLabels are keyed by bare name — legacy hierarchies never join parent to child, and same-named HLabels in different children short

**Severity:** HIGH (default path, every hierarchical legacy schematic)
**File:** `schematic/legacy_reader.py:707-720`, `:775-783` (`_parse_legacy_single_sheet`, the `$Sheet` loop keeps only F1 = the file name); `schematic/connectivity.py:489-491` (`build_net_map`, HLabels into `label_keys` under the bare name with no namespace; the legacy caller `schematic/pipeline.py:885-896` adds only `_sheet`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R2-F5) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `042d04f, 0dbd6ec` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** a legacy parent's sheet pins produce no port point, so a child's `HLabel VOUT` never reaches the parent net; two children each with an `HLabel EN` are merged into one net.
- **Fix:** Legacy `$Sheet` F2+ records become sheet pins, child HLabels are namespaced per instance, repeated sheets take per-instance `AR` references (ruling 6), and a recursive sheet reference stops with a `diagnostics` record. Corpus (class L3): 184 legacy units change `sheets_parsed` / `sheet_files` / component count (+8,317 components net over all legacy units); legacy LB-001 1,618 -> 6,202 as hierarchical ports now join (inside label L).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 664 OK (8 skips); `check_refactor.py quick` vs the `79420eb` snapshot 8/8 OK (fixture JSON deltas only in the declared classes, 2 allowed text artefacts); `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1`; kicad-cli / KiCad-5 netlist / DRC oracles (handoff-wave3.md). Harness: Wave 3 gate `004bba5`..`d2b9e72` — see status.md; per-unit labels `results/v30x_w3_gate/field_report_budgeted_v30x-wave3_streamed.units.jsonl`, class summary `results/v30x_w3_gate/class_summary.json`.

## 2026-10-26 — KH-514: same-name global bus labels never union their members — `global_label` on a bus falls to role `local` in the bus pass

**Severity:** HIGH (default path, designs that carry a bus across sheets on global labels)
**File:** `schematic/connectivity.py:456-463`, `:473-474` (`build_net_map`: a `global_label` gets role `"local"` and goes into `bus_label_idx`, skipping the global branch at :487); `:607-622` (`bus_slot`: members joined only via `label_keys.get((member, s))` / `member_rep[(s, member)]`, per sheet)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R2-F4) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `756339b, 9a5c90c, 5f6a734` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** a `D[0..7]` global bus label on two sheets leaves `D0`…`D7` as separate per-sheet nets; KiCad connects bus members across same-name global bus labels. No global-scope member union exists anywhere in the bus pass (:485-744).
- **Fix:** Global bus labels union their members across sheets (variant C); bus-entry tap lookup fixed (KH-670). Corpus (class M4): M4 (with KH-670): 753 modern units / 186 repos (bus_topology moved, or nets moved on a design with a global bus label).

## 2026-10-26 — KH-515: modern sub-symbol names `Name_<unit>_<bodystyle>` keep only the unit — De Morgan symbols get both body styles' pins

**Severity:** HIGH (default path, modern schematics with De Morgan symbols)
**File:** `schematic/reader.py:98-104` (`_extract_pins_from_node`, :100 keeps the unit only), `:187-195` (`compute_pin_positions`); no `convert` / `body_style` read anywhere in `schematic/` or `kicad_core/`
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R2-F3 modern half) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `1c0e975, 15d23b4` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** `VCAR.kicad_sch` `4xxx:4001` units each carry duplicate pins 1/2/3, 4/5/6 … (six entries for three pins); the alternate-body pins sit at other coordinates and can join wrong nets. Legacy twin: KH-512.
- **Fix:** Modern sub-symbol names keep the body style; only the placed symbol's body style contributes pins. Corpus (class M2): M2: 1,801 modern units / 375 repos; 56,346 duplicate (component, pin) net slots removed.

## 2026-10-26 — KH-516: `parse_value` rescales explicit-farad capacitor values as legacy pF/µF — `1F` → 1e-12, `120F` supercaps mis-scaled

**Severity:** HIGH (default path, every schematic with a farad-unit value)
**File:** `kicad_core/values.py:61` (`parse_value`: the unit strip loses the explicit `F`) → `:104-112` (legacy pF/µF rescale); docstring `:36-37` says only bare integers are rescaled
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R1-F2) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `6ad8fee, af31634` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** with `component_type="capacitor"`: `1F` → 1e-12, `0.1F` → 1e-7, `1e-6F` → 1e-12, `1 F` → 1e-12, `0.47F 5.5V` → 4.7e-7. The corpus has `120F` ×40, `1F` ×11, `40F` ×4, `0.3F`, `0.10F`, `1.5F`, `2.5F`, `20F`, `50F` (about 80 values); each one is off by 1e-12 or 1e-6 and feeds `parsed_values` → RC / derating / power math.
- **Fix:** An explicit (upper-case) `F` and a bare exponent are SI farads (ruling 8); only bare integers keep the legacy pF/µF rescale. Corpus (class M5): M5 (with KH-517): 29 modern units / 16 repos, 98 component `parsed_value` changes; EMC PDN recommendation text follows (downstream class D).
- **Verification:** Product-side: `tools/tests` 664 OK (8 skips); `check_refactor.py quick` vs the `79420eb` snapshot 8/8 OK (fixture JSON deltas only in the declared classes, 2 allowed text artefacts); `--schema` x6 byte-identical to `07b7fb1`; kicad-cli / KiCad-5 netlist / DRC oracles (handoff-wave3.md). Harness: Wave 3 gate `004bba5`..`d2b9e72` — see status.md; per-unit labels `results/v30x_w3_gate/field_report_budgeted_v30x-wave3_streamed.units.jsonl`, class summary `results/v30x_w3_gate/class_summary.json`.

## 2026-10-26 — KH-517: `snap_to_e_series` uses linear distance within the decade and the table has no 10.0 — values just under a decade snap down by up to 17 %

**Severity:** HIGH (what_if `--suggest-fixes` E-series suggestions and EMC cap recommendations)
**File:** `kicad_core/values.py:197-201` (`snap_to_e_series`; the comment at :190-196 says log-scale nearest neighbour); consumers `what_if.py:832`, `skills/emc/scripts/emc_formulas.py:574` (`round_to_e12`)
**Discovered:** 2026-10-25, external audit round 1 at `07b7fb1` (`docs/audit/02-v3-kicad-code/findings/VERIFICATION.md` kc/R1-F5) **Fixed:** product v3.0.x-dev `6ad8fee, af31634` (3.0.x Wave 3, unreleased).

- **Root cause:** `snap_to_e_series(9900,'E12')` → (8200, −17.17 %) where 10 k is nearer; `(9.6,'E24')` → 9.1 (10 is nearer); `(9.9,'E96')` → 9.76. The EMC skill bundle has the sibling note `round_to_e12(9.9 nF)` → 8.2 nF.
- **Fix:** `snap_to_e_series` picks the nearest value by log distance with the next decade's first value as a candidate. Corpus (class M5): M5 (with KH-516): 29 modern units / 16 repos, 98 `parsed_value` changes.
